about: Every field of a Scene layer's `rig` (rig.scene, rig.render and the Rig's own fields): type, range, default, what it does. Built from the engine by frontend/src/world3d/schema/build.mjs; do not edit by hand.

rig.doc: The Scene layer's `rig`: the backdrop, Rig lights, environment, look, render settings and the agent's world (`scene`).

renderer.doc: world: the 3D world renderer (needs WebGPU). classic: the old per-layer 3D pass. Write "world".

scene.doc: The world an agent writes on the Scene layer: `rig.scene`.

items.doc: One thing in the world: its geometry (`graph`, `model`, `splat` or `mesh`), where it stands, and what it is made of.

id.doc: A name, unique in the scene. `@id` in another graph, `parent`, focus and reports use it.

parent.doc: Another object's id: this one moves with it, `at`/`rot`/`scale` then in the parent's space. null: the root.

at.doc: Position, metres.

scale.doc: Scale: one number or [x, y, z].

material.doc: The name of a material in `scene.materials`. Undefined names render grey.

materials.doc: Materials by slot, for graphs that name regions (`assign`, `inset`, `decal`, `udim`): slot 0 first.

graph.doc: The geometry as a list of op nodes; the last node is the output. See the ops.

keys.doc: Tracks: `at`, `rot`, `scale`, `shape:<name>` (a shape key's weight) and `visible`: [{ "t": 0, "v": false }, { "t": 1.5, "v": true }] shows and hides the object (its children too) at those times, in Draft and Final: it is there or not, never half, and a frame's motion blur never spreads a switch (the frame's own time decides for its whole shutter). Before its first key it holds that key's value.

visible.doc: true: shown from this key on; false: hidden (it casts no shadow, shows in no reflection and gives no light).

of.doc: A field driven by a clock: { "clock": "move1", "map": [[u0, v0, ease], [u1, v1, ease], ...] } (or an expression of several: { "expr", "vars" }), or a list of such terms, which combine: `scale` multiplies them, every other field adds them (a logo that grows in on move1 and shrinks out on move2 is two terms). With keys on the same field the keys' value combines with them the same way.

clock.doc: The name of a clock in `scene.clocks`.

map.doc: The remap from the clock's value u to the field's value: [[u0, v0, ease], [u1, v1, ease], ...], u rising, v the field's shape (a number, or [x, y, z] for `at` and `rot`), ease the curve from that point to the next (any name or [x1, y1, x2, y2] a key's `ease` takes; `linear` for a part that should follow u exactly). Below the first u it holds v0, above the last the last v. Left out: the value is u itself.

expr.doc: Instead of `clock` and `map`: an expression of the Video Editor's ƒx language (the Custom ƒx's: + - * / ^, sin, cos, lerp, clamp, ...) over `vars` and `time` (seconds on the Scene's clock), as a Blender driver's scripted expression. A number, or [x, y, z] for `at` and `rot`: "[r * cos(a), 0.8 * r * sin(a), 0]", "(1.38 + 1.34 * z) * (1.015 - 0.003 * time)". One that does not parse or run is named in the render's warnings and leaves the field to its keys or its value.

of.doc: A number, or { clock, map }: that clock through its own remap.

clock.doc: The name of a clock in `scene.clocks`.

map.doc: The remap from the clock's value to the variable's: [[u0, v0, ease], ...], as a term's `map`. Left out: the clock's value itself.

vars.doc: The expression's variables by name: { "r": { "clock": "move1", "map": [[0.8, 0.06, "appleOut"], [0.97, 0]] }, "k": 2 }. A name the language already has (time, sin, PI, ...) is not a variable.

items.doc: One term: { clock, map }.

clock.doc: The name of a clock in `scene.clocks`.

map.doc: The remap from the clock's value u to the field's value: [[u0, v0, ease], [u1, v1, ease], ...], u rising, v the field's shape (a number, or [x, y, z] for `at` and `rot`), ease the curve from that point to the next (any name or [x1, y1, x2, y2] a key's `ease` takes; `linear` for a part that should follow u exactly). Below the first u it holds v0, above the last the last v. Left out: the value is u itself.

expr.doc: Instead of `clock` and `map`: an expression of the Video Editor's ƒx language (the Custom ƒx's: + - * / ^, sin, cos, lerp, clamp, ...) over `vars` and `time` (seconds on the Scene's clock), as a Blender driver's scripted expression. A number, or [x, y, z] for `at` and `rot`: "[r * cos(a), 0.8 * r * sin(a), 0]", "(1.38 + 1.34 * z) * (1.015 - 0.003 * time)". One that does not parse or run is named in the render's warnings and leaves the field to its keys or its value.

of.doc: A number, or { clock, map }: that clock through its own remap.

clock.doc: The name of a clock in `scene.clocks`.

map.doc: The remap from the clock's value to the variable's: [[u0, v0, ease], ...], as a term's `map`. Left out: the clock's value itself.

vars.doc: The expression's variables by name: { "r": { "clock": "move1", "map": [[0.8, 0.06, "appleOut"], [0.97, 0]] }, "k": 2 }. A name the language already has (time, sin, PI, ...) is not a variable.

drive.doc: Fields driven by the scene's clocks: { "<field>": { "clock": "move1", "map": [[u0, v0, ease], ...] } } (or a list of terms), for `at`, `rot`, `scale`, `shape:<name>`, and a path's `along` and `bank`. See `scene.clocks`.

of.doc: One of the Video Editor's keyframe expressions (ƒx) on this field's keys, the very functions a layer's track runs: { "glide": "soft" }, { "spring": "snappy" }, { "wiggle": { "amp": 2, "freq": 1.5 } }, { "custom": "value + 0.02 * sin(time * 4)" }. One a field; a vector field takes it on each of its numbers.

elastic.doc: Elastic: reshapes each key's move into a springy one that overshoots and wobbles into place: { amp [100] %, freq [1.1] wobbles across the move, decay [5] }. true takes the defaults.

spring.doc: Spring: each key's move is a real spring in seconds: "snappy", "gentle" or { amp [100] %, freq [1.6] Hz, damping [0.55] }. true takes the defaults.

bounce.doc: Bounce: each key's move falls onto its value and rebounds in decaying hops: { amp [100] %, elasticity [45] %, bounces [5] }. true takes the defaults.

wiggle.doc: Wiggle: adds smooth noise around the keyed value: { amp (the field's own units; ten of its steps: 1 cm, 2 degrees, 0.02 of scale), freq [3] Hz }. true takes the defaults.

glide.doc: Glide: softens the keyed move (its eases included) through the editor's Glide: a fast response plus a slow tail, so it lands soft and keeps creeping on, never past the key and never back. A preset by name ("soft", "floaty", "trailing", "endless") or { fast [0.1] s, slow [0.6] s, weight [25] % of every move the tail carries, delay [0] s }. true takes the defaults.

weight.doc: Tail Share (%).

custom.doc: Custom: replaces the value with an expression of the editor's ƒx language (`value`, `time`, `frame`, `wiggle()`, `loopOut()`, `valueAtTime()`, `glide()`, ...): the text, or { code }. true takes the defaults.

fx.doc: The Video Editor's ƒx on a field's keys: { "<field>": { "glide": "soft" } }, for `at`, `rot`, `scale`, `shape:<name>`, `along` and `bank`.

path.doc: Follow path: the object rides a curve through `points` (metres, in its parent's space, measured from its own `at`). `along` 0 is the first point and 1 the last, by the share of the curve's length, so a linear `along` is an even speed; key it (`keys.along`) or drive it (`drive.along`) with any ease.

points.doc: The curve's points, two or more: [[x, y, z], ...]. The curve passes through each one.

tension.doc: How the curve bends between points: 0.5 a Catmull-Rom spline (smooth), 0 straight lines from point to point.

closed.doc: The last point joins the first: `along` past 1 goes round again.

along.doc: Where on the curve the object stands: the share of its length from the first point. Keyable and drivable (`keys.along`, `drive.along`).

orient.doc: Turn the object along the curve: its +Z runs the way the curve goes, its +Y toward `up`. Its own `rot` then turns it within that frame.

up.doc: With `orient`: which way the object's top leans.

bank.doc: With `orient`: a roll about the direction of travel, degrees. Keyable and drivable (`keys.bank`).

shapes.doc: Shape key weights without a track: { "open": 0.4 }.

castShadow.doc: false: throws no shadow (Draft and Final).

tags.doc: Names for light and shadow linking: a light's `lights`, `excludes`, `shadowFrom` and `shadowExcludes` pick objects by them. A child has its parents' tags too. An object with no tags is lit only by lights with no `lights` list.

visibility.doc: Which kinds of rays see the object; each true unless set false. `camera`: false leaves it out of the picture but in its shadows and reflections (a bounce card that must not show). `shadow`: false is `castShadow: false`. `reflection`, `refraction`, `indirect`: whether it shows in glossy reflections, through glass, and in the light bounced off matte surfaces (Final; Draft traces no such rays).

camera.doc: Seen by the camera (Draft and Final).

shadow.doc: Throws shadows (Draft and Final): the same as `castShadow`.

reflection.doc: Seen in glossy reflections: mirrors, chrome, glass's reflection, a lacquer (Final).

indirect.doc: Its light bounced onto matte surfaces, and what they bounce onto it (Final).

holdout.doc: true: the object cuts a hole in the picture where the camera sees it: those pixels are see-through (alpha 0), so the layers below the Scene show there, as a matte for compositing. It still hides what is behind it, still casts its shadow and still shows in reflections, in Draft and Final. A holdout floor under a product keeps the shadow off: for a floor that shows only its shadow use `catcher`.

model.doc: A .glb/.gltf file to show instead of a graph. It keeps its own materials, unless the object names a `material`: then every mesh of the file wears that one (a texture graph, an animated one too, bakes on each mesh's own atlas).

rigid.doc: Makes the object a rigid body that falls, hits and stacks (true for the defaults).

keyed.doc: Follows the object's keys and pushes what is in the way.

shape.doc: Collision shape. `mesh` only for fixed bodies.

start.doc: Seconds to hold it in the air before it falls.

catcher.doc: A shadow catcher: the surface shows only the shadows on it ({ "tint": "#000", "strength": 1 }).

light.doc: Also takes the objects' light onto it (their bounce and reflections), in Final: 0 off.

portal.doc: true: an opening the environment's light comes in through (the window or open door of a closed room): a flat `plane` the size of the opening at its inner face. Never drawn, casts nothing, does nothing without an environment; in Final the environment's light samples aim through the portals (up to 8). Leave it out of open sets.

baked.doc: Geometry the editor or a .blend import hands over by name.

mesh.doc: Finished geometry from a binary file: { url, position: [offset, length], normal, uv, index, indexType }.

placements.doc: A .blend import's instance placements ([offset, length] in its geometry file).

copies.doc: How many copies a .blend import's scattered object has.

sim.removed: An object's own `sim` is gone: write cloth and soft bodies as `scene.sims`.

skeleton.doc: Bones and skin weights made for a mesh that has none (a graph's mesh, a model file without a skeleton). The mesh is then a skinned character like any file with a skeleton: `pose` moves its joints (clips, bones, IK, look-at), Draft skins it and Final traces it skinned. Joints come from a `template` placed by `landmarks` (the ones left out are found from the mesh's shape: a standing figure facing +Z, its left at +X, arms out in a T or A pose or hanging clear of the body at its sides), or are written out in `joints`, or both. Weights are made by heat diffusion over the surface (nothing leaks across a gap: two legs, two fingers), then `fixes` edit them. The scene report (`inspect`) lists the joints, the landmarks it found and the checks.

template.doc: A ready joint tree. biped: hips, spine, chest, neck, head; upperArm, forearm, hand; thigh, shin, foot, toe (.L and .R). quadruped: hips, spine, chest, neck, head, tail; upperArm, forearm, frontFoot; thigh, shin, hindFoot (.L and .R).

landmarks.doc: Points of the body by name. biped: hips, spine, chest, neck, head, headTop, shoulder, elbow, wrist, handTip, hip, knee, ankle, ball, toe (the last ten with .L / .R). quadruped: hips, spine, chest, neck, head, nose, tail, tailTip, shoulder, elbow, wrist, frontFoot, hip, knee, hock, hindFoot (.L / .R). Each one left out is found from the shape.

symmetric.doc: A ".L" landmark given (or found) alone also places its ".R" mirrored across the middle.

items.doc: One joint: where it turns, what it hangs from.

name.doc: Its name: the pose's bones, masks and constraints use it. A template's joint of the same name is replaced.

parent.doc: The joint it hangs from; null (or left out): a root.

at.doc: Where it turns, in the mesh's own space.

tail.doc: Where a joint with no children ends (fingertips, the top of the head): its bone runs from `at` to here.

rot.doc: Its rest turn, degrees XYZ. Left out: its axes are the mesh's, so `rot: [x, 0, 0]` in a pose turns it about the mesh's X.

joints.doc: Joints written out: the whole tree without a template, or joints a template's are replaced by or added to (fingers, ears, a tail).

bind.doc: `skin`: smooth weights that bend the surface at the joints. `rigid`: every connected part follows the one joint that holds most of it (a robot of separate parts).

skinning.doc: How the joints move the skin. `dualQuaternion`: each point follows a blend of its joints' motions that is itself a rigid motion, so a bent elbow keeps its thickness and a twisted wrist does not collapse; a joint's scale scales its part of the skin about the joint, as linear blending does. `linear`: the joints' matrices averaged, as a file's own skeleton is drawn (a 90-degree bend thins to 0.71 at the crease, a half-turn twist collapses).

parts.doc: A model file's meshes by name, each following one joint whole: { "Helmet": "head" }.

smooth.doc: Blur passes over the whole surface after the solve.

threshold.doc: A joint's share under this is dropped (four joints a vertex at most, the rest shared out).

visibility.doc: A point is heated only by bones it can see from inside the body (what keeps weights from leaking across gaps).

items.doc: A manual weight edit, applied in order after the automatic weights: a joint's weight set (or added, multiplied, raised, lowered) over a region, the other joints sharing what is left as they did. Or `smooth` passes that blur every joint's weights over the region. Regions combine (all of them at once).

joint.doc: The joint whose weight the fix sets.

value.doc: The weight it sets (or adds, multiplies by, at least, at most).

mode.doc: How `value` acts on the joint's weight.

smooth.doc: Blur passes instead of a value: every joint's weights move toward their neighbours' in the region.

group.doc: A vertex group of the graph's mesh (weightGradient, weightProximity, weightMask, weightNoise wrote it): as much as the group's weight.

mesh.doc: A model file's mesh by name: all of it.

of.doc: The points a joint holds most now (fix a joint's own region).

box.doc: The points inside a box (with `soft` metres of fade outside it).

sphere.doc: The points inside a ball (fading over its last `soft` metres).

at.doc: Centre.

near.doc: A brush: all of it within `inner` of the point, fading to nothing at `radius` by `falloff`.

at.doc: Centre.

soft.doc: Fade at the edge of a `box` or `sphere`, metres.

strength.doc: How much of the fix applies (times the region's own share).

items.doc: An animation made of keys on the joints, played by the pose like a file's own clip (`pose.clips: [{ "clip": "<name>" }]`: crossfades, loops, root motion). Keys are in the clip's own seconds; it is sampled 60 times a second, so each key's ease plays as written.

duration.doc: Its length, seconds. Left out: its last key.

of.doc: A joint's tracks.

items.doc: One key: `t` seconds on the scene's clock, `v` the value, `ease` the curve from this key to the next.

t.doc: Seconds from the Scene clip's start. A key before 0 starts a move already under way when the clip starts (an entry that is moving on its first frame).

v.doc: The value at `t`: a number or an [x, y, z] list, the same shape as the field it keys.

ease.doc: How the move from this key to the next eases. A name: the world's `linear`, `in`, `out`, `inOut`, `back`, `bounce` (cubic power curves), or any keyframe easing of the Video Editor, the very curve it plays, by id (`aeSmooth`, `aeIn`, `aeOut`, `natural`, `appleOut`, `smoothGlide`, `punch`, `power`, `expoOut`, `backOut`, `overshoot`, ...) or by the name its keys write (`AE Smooth`); `hold` stays on this key's value until the next key. Or your own curve, the editor's Custom: [x1, y1, x2, y2] as in CSS cubic-bezier(), x the share of the time between the keys (0 to 1), y the share of the move (-3 to 4: below 0 or above 1 overshoots).

rot.doc: Turn from the joint's rest, degrees XYZ, each `v` [x, y, z].

items.doc: One key: `t` seconds on the scene's clock, `v` the value, `ease` the curve from this key to the next.

t.doc: Seconds from the Scene clip's start. A key before 0 starts a move already under way when the clip starts (an entry that is moving on its first frame).

v.doc: The value at `t`: a number or an [x, y, z] list, the same shape as the field it keys.

ease.doc: How the move from this key to the next eases. A name: the world's `linear`, `in`, `out`, `inOut`, `back`, `bounce` (cubic power curves), or any keyframe easing of the Video Editor, the very curve it plays, by id (`aeSmooth`, `aeIn`, `aeOut`, `natural`, `appleOut`, `smoothGlide`, `punch`, `power`, `expoOut`, `backOut`, `overshoot`, ...) or by the name its keys write (`AE Smooth`); `hold` stays on this key's value until the next key. Or your own curve, the editor's Custom: [x1, y1, x2, y2] as in CSS cubic-bezier(), x the share of the time between the keys (0 to 1), y the share of the move (-3 to 4: below 0 or above 1 overshoots).

at.doc: Move from its rest, in its parent's frame (the mesh's units), each `v` [x, y, z].

items.doc: One key: `t` seconds on the scene's clock, `v` the value, `ease` the curve from this key to the next.

t.doc: Seconds from the Scene clip's start. A key before 0 starts a move already under way when the clip starts (an entry that is moving on its first frame).

v.doc: The value at `t`: a number or an [x, y, z] list, the same shape as the field it keys.

ease.doc: How the move from this key to the next eases. A name: the world's `linear`, `in`, `out`, `inOut`, `back`, `bounce` (cubic power curves), or any keyframe easing of the Video Editor, the very curve it plays, by id (`aeSmooth`, `aeIn`, `aeOut`, `natural`, `appleOut`, `smoothGlide`, `punch`, `power`, `expoOut`, `backOut`, `overshoot`, ...) or by the name its keys write (`AE Smooth`); `hold` stays on this key's value until the next key. Or your own curve, the editor's Custom: [x1, y1, x2, y2] as in CSS cubic-bezier(), x the share of the time between the keys (0 to 1), y the share of the move (-3 to 4: below 0 or above 1 overshoots).

scale.doc: Scale, each `v` a number or [x, y, z].

clips.doc: Animations made of keys on the joints.

pose.doc: The pose of an object with a `skeleton`: the same pipeline as a model layer's `model3dConfig.pose` (clips, morphs, bones, constraints, layers, in that order), on the Scene's clock. Its clips are the skeleton's own `clips`.

order.doc: The pipeline's order, stored with the project: clips, morphs, bones, constraints, world. It is the only order there is; another is ignored with a warning.

items.doc: One of the file's animations, playing. The first clip is the base; each next one is laid over what is below by its weight (0..1): a crossfade is the next clip's `fadeIn` while the one before keeps playing. Before `start` and after `end` a clip lays nothing.

clip.doc: The animation's name in the file (the layer's pose report lists them). A name the file does not have is skipped with a warning, so a re-imported file keeps the pose.

end.doc: Layer seconds when it stops (null: never).

fadeIn.doc: Seconds it takes to rise to its weight after `start` (an S-curve, so the blend starts and ends gently).

fadeOut.doc: Seconds it takes to fall to 0 before `end`.

weight.doc: How much of it lies over what is below: 1 replaces, 0.5 is halfway.

time.doc: The clip's own time, set outright (key it to scrub the clip by hand); `speed` and `offset` then do nothing.

blend.doc: `add` lays the clip's change from the file's rest pose on top instead of replacing (a breathing clip over a walk).

clips.doc: The clips, the first one the base.

root.doc: Root motion: "normal" (the clip moves the character as it was made), "inPlace" (its travel along the ground taken out, up and down kept), "accumulate" (a looping clip carries on from where the last loop ended). Or { mode, bone } to name the root bone (left out: the top bone a clip moves).

mode.doc: The root motion.

bone.doc: The root bone.

of.doc: A morph target's weight, by name: a number, or { value, mode, weight, mesh, keys }.

value.doc: The weight it sets (0 none, 1 the whole target).

mode.doc: `replace` sets it over what the clips made; `add` adds to it.

weight.doc: How much of the control applies.

mesh.doc: Only on this mesh (by node name); left out: every mesh with a target of that name.

of.doc: A bone's (or any node's) local transform, by name, over what the clips and morphs made.

rot.doc: Rotation, degrees XYZ, in the bone's own frame (its local axes).

at.doc: Position in the bone's parent's units (`add`: an offset).

mode.doc: `add` turns, moves and scales on top of the animation; `replace` sets the local transform, blended by `weight`.

weight.doc: How much of it applies.

items.doc: A constraint, solved after the clips, morphs and bones, against the layer's world transform of this frame. `type` picks the fields: lookAt (aim a bone at a target), ik (two-bone IK: the bone's parent and grandparent bend so the bone reaches a target), parent (a bone held by a target), path (a bone moved along points), attach (a Scene object held by a bone).

bone.doc: The bone it acts on (attach: the bone that holds).

weight.doc: How much of it applies: key 0 → 1 to hand a bone from its animation to the constraint (space switching).

target.doc: What it looks at. "@id" (or "id") a Scene object, as it stands at the Scene's time; [x, y, z] a point in the Scene's metres (the editor's 3D space: one composition pixel is a millimetre); { "bone": "<name>" } one of this model's own bones.

bone.doc: A bone (or any node) of this model, by name.

chain.doc: How many bones share the turn, the bone and its parents (2: neck and head).

limit.doc: The most it turns from the animated pose, degrees.

axis.doc: The bone's front in its own frame. Left out: the model's front (+Z of the file, or `forward`) as the bone holds it at rest.

forward.doc: The model's front in the file's frame, for the default `axis`.

target.doc: What the bone reaches for (out of reach: the arm points at it, straight). "@id" (or "id") a Scene object, as it stands at the Scene's time; [x, y, z] a point in the Scene's metres (the editor's 3D space: one composition pixel is a millimetre); { "bone": "<name>" } one of this model's own bones.

bone.doc: A bone (or any node) of this model, by name.

pole.doc: Where the middle joint (elbow, knee) bends toward. Left out: the bend the pose already has. "@id" (or "id") a Scene object, as it stands at the Scene's time; [x, y, z] a point in the Scene's metres (the editor's 3D space: one composition pixel is a millimetre); { "bone": "<name>" } one of this model's own bones.

bone.doc: A bone (or any node) of this model, by name.

tip.doc: A bone under `bone` (a fingertip, a toe) that lands on the target instead of the end's own origin, so a hand touches what it reaches rather than going through it.

target.doc: What holds the bone. "@id" (or "id") a Scene object, as it stands at the Scene's time; [x, y, z] a point in the Scene's metres (the editor's 3D space: one composition pixel is a millimetre); { "bone": "<name>" } one of this model's own bones.

bone.doc: A bone (or any node) of this model, by name.

at.doc: Offset in the target's (or the bone's) frame, metres.

rot.doc: Turn in that frame, degrees XYZ.

items.doc: A point of the path. "@id" (or "id") a Scene object, as it stands at the Scene's time; [x, y, z] a point in the Scene's metres (the editor's 3D space: one composition pixel is a millimetre); { "bone": "<name>" } one of this model's own bones.

bone.doc: A bone (or any node) of this model, by name.

path.doc: At least two points (a smooth curve through them).

progress.doc: Where along the path, 0 its start to 1 its end (key it).

orient.doc: Turn the bone's front along the path.

axis.doc: The bone's front in its own frame, for `orient`.

forward.doc: The model's front, for the default axis.

object.doc: The Scene object (`rig.scene.objects[].id`, "@id" too) the bone holds. It is drawn there in Draft and Final; with `weight` below 1 it is part way between its own place and the hand.

at.doc: Offset in the target's (or the bone's) frame, metres.

rot.doc: Turn in that frame, degrees XYZ.

keep.doc: Hold the object where it was against the bone at the moment it is picked up (`grab`), instead of at `at`/`rot`: key `weight` 0 → 1 when the hand reaches it and it never jumps.

grab.doc: Layer seconds of the pick-up for `keep`. Left out: where `weight` starts to rise (the last 0 key before the first one above).

items.doc: An animation layer: its own clips, morphs, bones and constraints, each laid in its step over the pose below, by its weight, through its mask.

on.doc: false: the layer is left out (kept in the project).

weight.doc: How much of the layer lies over what is below.

mask.doc: Where a layer may write. Every list left out lets everything through. Bones and objects take their children too (`children: false` only the named ones).

bones.doc: Bones (and everything under them) the layer moves.

objects.doc: Nodes of the file by name (a mesh, a group), with what is under them.

exclude.doc: Bones or nodes (and their children) the layer never touches, inside the ones above.

children.doc: false: `bones` and `objects` mean only the named nodes.

items.doc: One property.

properties.doc: The properties it writes: rotation, position, scale, morphs.

morphs.doc: Morph targets by name the layer sets.

items.doc: One of the file's animations, playing. The first clip is the base; each next one is laid over what is below by its weight (0..1): a crossfade is the next clip's `fadeIn` while the one before keeps playing. Before `start` and after `end` a clip lays nothing.

clip.doc: The animation's name in the file (the layer's pose report lists them). A name the file does not have is skipped with a warning, so a re-imported file keeps the pose.

end.doc: Layer seconds when it stops (null: never).

fadeIn.doc: Seconds it takes to rise to its weight after `start` (an S-curve, so the blend starts and ends gently).

fadeOut.doc: Seconds it takes to fall to 0 before `end`.

weight.doc: How much of it lies over what is below: 1 replaces, 0.5 is halfway.

time.doc: The clip's own time, set outright (key it to scrub the clip by hand); `speed` and `offset` then do nothing.

blend.doc: `add` lays the clip's change from the file's rest pose on top instead of replacing (a breathing clip over a walk).

clips.doc: Clips laid over by this layer.

of.doc: A morph target's weight, by name: a number, or { value, mode, weight, mesh, keys }.

value.doc: The weight it sets (0 none, 1 the whole target).

mode.doc: `replace` sets it over what the clips made; `add` adds to it.

weight.doc: How much of the control applies.

mesh.doc: Only on this mesh (by node name); left out: every mesh with a target of that name.

of.doc: A bone's (or any node's) local transform, by name, over what the clips and morphs made.

rot.doc: Rotation, degrees XYZ, in the bone's own frame (its local axes).

at.doc: Position in the bone's parent's units (`add`: an offset).

mode.doc: `add` turns, moves and scales on top of the animation; `replace` sets the local transform, blended by `weight`.

weight.doc: How much of it applies.

items.doc: A constraint, solved after the clips, morphs and bones, against the layer's world transform of this frame. `type` picks the fields: lookAt (aim a bone at a target), ik (two-bone IK: the bone's parent and grandparent bend so the bone reaches a target), parent (a bone held by a target), path (a bone moved along points), attach (a Scene object held by a bone).

bone.doc: The bone it acts on (attach: the bone that holds).

weight.doc: How much of it applies: key 0 → 1 to hand a bone from its animation to the constraint (space switching).

target.doc: What it looks at. "@id" (or "id") a Scene object, as it stands at the Scene's time; [x, y, z] a point in the Scene's metres (the editor's 3D space: one composition pixel is a millimetre); { "bone": "<name>" } one of this model's own bones.

bone.doc: A bone (or any node) of this model, by name.

chain.doc: How many bones share the turn, the bone and its parents (2: neck and head).

limit.doc: The most it turns from the animated pose, degrees.

axis.doc: The bone's front in its own frame. Left out: the model's front (+Z of the file, or `forward`) as the bone holds it at rest.

forward.doc: The model's front in the file's frame, for the default `axis`.

target.doc: What the bone reaches for (out of reach: the arm points at it, straight). "@id" (or "id") a Scene object, as it stands at the Scene's time; [x, y, z] a point in the Scene's metres (the editor's 3D space: one composition pixel is a millimetre); { "bone": "<name>" } one of this model's own bones.

bone.doc: A bone (or any node) of this model, by name.

pole.doc: Where the middle joint (elbow, knee) bends toward. Left out: the bend the pose already has. "@id" (or "id") a Scene object, as it stands at the Scene's time; [x, y, z] a point in the Scene's metres (the editor's 3D space: one composition pixel is a millimetre); { "bone": "<name>" } one of this model's own bones.

bone.doc: A bone (or any node) of this model, by name.

tip.doc: A bone under `bone` (a fingertip, a toe) that lands on the target instead of the end's own origin, so a hand touches what it reaches rather than going through it.

target.doc: What holds the bone. "@id" (or "id") a Scene object, as it stands at the Scene's time; [x, y, z] a point in the Scene's metres (the editor's 3D space: one composition pixel is a millimetre); { "bone": "<name>" } one of this model's own bones.

bone.doc: A bone (or any node) of this model, by name.

at.doc: Offset in the target's (or the bone's) frame, metres.

rot.doc: Turn in that frame, degrees XYZ.

items.doc: A point of the path. "@id" (or "id") a Scene object, as it stands at the Scene's time; [x, y, z] a point in the Scene's metres (the editor's 3D space: one composition pixel is a millimetre); { "bone": "<name>" } one of this model's own bones.

bone.doc: A bone (or any node) of this model, by name.

path.doc: At least two points (a smooth curve through them).

progress.doc: Where along the path, 0 its start to 1 its end (key it).

orient.doc: Turn the bone's front along the path.

axis.doc: The bone's front in its own frame, for `orient`.

forward.doc: The model's front, for the default axis.

object.doc: The Scene object (`rig.scene.objects[].id`, "@id" too) the bone holds. It is drawn there in Draft and Final; with `weight` below 1 it is part way between its own place and the hand.

at.doc: Offset in the target's (or the bone's) frame, metres.

rot.doc: Turn in that frame, degrees XYZ.

keep.doc: Hold the object where it was against the bone at the moment it is picked up (`grab`), instead of at `at`/`rot`: key `weight` 0 → 1 when the hand reaches it and it never jumps.

grab.doc: Layer seconds of the pick-up for `keep`. Left out: where `weight` starts to rise (the last 0 key before the first one above).

layers.doc: Animation layers, after the pose's own entries, in order.

of.doc: A surface. Every field is optional; a material with nothing set is light grey plastic (roughness 0.5).

base.doc: The surface colour (sRGB). It multiplies `maps.base` and a procedural pattern's colours, so leave it out to show a picture as it is.

roughness.doc: 0 is a mirror finish, 1 fully matte. On glass it frosts the glass.

metalness.doc: 1 is metal (the colour tints the reflection), 0 is not. Prefer `metal` for real metals.

specular.doc: Strength of the non-metal reflection. 1 is physical; 0 leaves only diffuse colour; up to 2 brightens it (a .blend import may write that).

coat.doc: A clear lacquer layer on top (car paint, varnished wood).

coatRoughness.doc: How rough the lacquer layer is.

preset.doc: A material from the library (over a hundred, made here: metals by their real n and k, glass, gems and liquids, plastics, car paints with flakes and orange peel, wood, stone, ceramic, cloth, glows, toon, dusty): its fields under the material's own, so `{ "preset": "carPaintRed", "base": "#1e4d2b" }` is a green car paint. The list and a contact sheet: world3d.md.

flakes.doc: Metallic flakes in the paint under the coat (car paint, a phone's back): a number 0 to 1 (how many and how bright) or { amount [0.6], size [0.15] mm, spread [18] degrees each flake's tilt, seed }. Each flake glints on its own where the light catches it, so the highlight sparkles and a sparkle runs across the body. Unset `metalness` becomes 0.35 + 0.6 × amount and `roughness` 0.32 (the flakes' own). Follows the mesh's uv in metres (`uvBox` on solids). Final traces every flake; Draft shows their average sheen. Replaces `maps.normal`.

amount.doc: How many flakes and how bright, 0 to 1.

spread.doc: How far each flake tilts from the surface, degrees.

coatBump.doc: The clear coat's own relief, "orange peel": a number 0 to 1 or { amount [0.4], scale [4] mm, seed }. The lacquer's reflection wobbles softly while the paint under it keeps its own; needs `coat`. 0.2 to 0.4 a factory finish, 0.7 a cheap respray. Draft and Final.

amount.doc: How strong the orange peel is, 0 to 1.

toon.doc: Toon (cel) shading with outlines, for motion design: true or { steps [3] flat bands of light, shade [0.35] the darkest band as a share of the colour, outline [true], outlineWidth [2] px, outlineColor ["#000000"] }. The surface takes its light in hard bands of `base`, and an outline follows its silhouette and creases at a constant width on screen. Draft and Final draw it the same (cel shading is the raster's; in Final the object still casts its traced shadow and bounces its colour onto the set). Other surface fields (`coat`, `metal`, maps but `base`) do not apply.

shade.doc: The darkest band as a share of the colour.

dust.doc: Dust settled on what faces up: a number 0 to 1 or { amount [0.5], color ["#c9c2b4"], up [0.5] how far from straight up it still settles (1 down to the sides), seed }. Lighter and matte, in soft patches, thinner on steeper faces, following each object's shape and where it stands (a per-object texture graph of the material's own `base`, `roughness` and `metalness`). For a material without `graph` (a preset's own dirt and dust are its params). A `coat` stays glossy over it: lower `coat` on a dusty car. Draft and Final.

up.doc: How far from straight up it still settles: 0 only flat tops, 1 down to the sides.

sheen.doc: Soft velvet rim light at grazing angles: cloth, felt, peach skin.

sheenRoughness.doc: How wide the sheen rim spreads.

transmission.doc: Glass and liquids: the share of light that passes through the surface and refracts. 1 with `roughness` 0 is clear glass; with `ior` and `attenuation*` it is a liquid. Final traces it for real; Draft shows it bent and tinted, a little milky.

ior.doc: Index of refraction of a transmissive or coated surface: 1.33 water, 1.36 alcohol/perfume, 1.45 oil, 1.5 glass, 2.42 diamond; 1 is a soap film over air.

thinWalled.doc: Whether glass is a thin wall or a solid body. Unset (the default) the mesh decides: on a closed mesh (a ball, a bottle with its walls, an ice cube, the water in a glass) a transmissive surface is a solid body, light bends going in and coming out (a ball lens turns the view over, caustics), as in Cycles; on an open mesh (a plane, a single-surface cup, a leaf) it is a thin wall that tints and reflects but bends nothing. `true` makes it a thin wall on any mesh (a soap bubble, a light bulb or a Christmas bauble modelled as one closed surface); `false` a solid body on any mesh (a sea or a pool's surface made of a plane, a half-space of water). Final and Draft alike.

thickness.removed: whether glass is a solid body or a thin wall is decided by its mesh now (closed: a solid body; open: a thin wall), and `thinWalled` decides it outright.

attenuationColor.doc: The colour light takes on after travelling `attenuationDistance` metres inside a transmissive body: the tint of a liquid or coloured glass. White is clear.

attenuationDistance.doc: Metres of the body after which light has the `attenuationColor` (Beer–Lambert: after d metres each channel keeps attenuationColor^(d / attenuationDistance)). Short distances against the object's size turn it dark: for a 10 cm bottle of perfume 0.2 to 0.5 reads light amber, 0.08 to 0.1 deep amber, 0.03 nearly black. Unset is no absorption (clear). Final only: Draft does not show it.

dispersion.doc: Glass that splits white light into colours (Final only, traced one wavelength a path): 20 / the Abbe number, so crown glass 0.34, flint 0.5 to 0.6, diamond 0.36 (with `ior` 2.42). A gem close-up wants 512 to 2048 samples.

priority.doc: Nested media: where two transmissive objects overlap (a liquid inside its glass, ice in a drink), the higher priority is what is there. Give the liquid 2 and the glass 1, and let the liquid touch or slightly overlap the glass walls: no air gap.

transmissionMean.doc: Written by a .blend import: the mean of a transmission map, for the preview's see-through strength.

emission.doc: Light the surface gives off, in this colour (black is none): screens, bulbs, neon, embers. With `emissionStrength` it lights the scene in Final; Draft shows it glowing. Or a colour temperature as "2700K": a black body's colour, luminance 1 (a filament, a candle flame "1900K").

emissionStrength.doc: Multiplies `emission`. 1 is a dim glow; 5 to 20 lights a room in Final; a phone screen is about 2 to 4. Below the scene's light it reads as paint, not as a lamp.

alpha.doc: Opacity: 1 solid, 0 invisible. For see-through glass use `transmission`, not alpha.

alphaFromBase.doc: Read the opacity from `maps.base`'s own alpha channel (a logo with see-through parts on a decal).

alphaMode.doc: How a cut (`maps.alpha` or `alphaFromBase`) is drawn. `blend`: see-through by its alpha, sorted (glass-like decals). `hash`: dithered in Draft, no sorting (overlapping petals, leaves, hair cards; Blender's Dithered). `clip`: solid where the alpha is over `alphaCutoff`, gone under it, in Draft and Final (a crisp cut-out). Final traces `blend` and `hash` by their exact coverage, as Cycles does.

alphaCutoff.doc: With `alphaMode` clip: the alpha under which the surface is gone.

doubleSided.doc: Draw both sides of every triangle. Sheets (planes, petals, ribbons, cloth) need it; closed solids do not.

pane.doc: Thin window glass (a pane in a frame): smooth, flat and clear. In Final the sky's and the sun's light come through it for every kind of ray (less its reflection), it reflects the room faintly, and a room's window portals stay open behind it: no caustic specks, no dark room behind glass. Draft shows it as clear glass. Give it to the `room` op's `glass` part. Its colour, roughness and transmission are fixed (only `ior`, 1.52 by default).

fabric.doc: Cloth that reads as cloth: the threads' relief, the crevices between them and each thread's own tint, at a scale no texture bake can hold, with a cloth's response (a soft sheen at grazing angles, a weak specular, fully rough; the material's own `sheen`, `specular`, `roughness` win). In the mesh's own uv in metres (every op's mesh has it). Final traces the threads at every sample, so they average over a pixel as a camera averages them; Draft draws them and fades them out where a thread is narrower than half a pixel (no shimmer, no moiré). The cloth's colour from afar stays the material's colour. Goes over a texture graph (`graph`: its wear, grime and colour) or a plain `base`. true is a plain weave at 300 threads a metre.

weave.doc: plain linen and cotton, twill (diagonal: denim, upholstery), basket (two by two: woven upholstery), knit (a throw, a jumper: V stitches in columns), pile (a wool rug's tufts, velvet, towelling).

threads.doc: Threads (stitches, tufts) per metre: fine linen 300 to 600, upholstery 150 to 300, a chunky knit 60 to 120, a rug's pile 300 to 800.

relief.doc: How proud the threads stand: 0 flat, 1 a real weave, 2 a coarse one.

contrast.doc: How dark the crevices between threads are.

variation.doc: How much each thread's shade differs (heathered yarn).

maps.doc: Pictures on the surface, each a media URL (`/media/…png`). They follow the mesh's uvs (give solids `uvBox`, `uvPlanar`, `uvCylinder` or `unwrap`).

normal.doc: A tangent-space normal map. `normalStrength` scales it; `normalFlipY` for maps made for DirectX.

roughness.doc: Roughness as grey; `roughness` then defaults to 1 and scales it.

metalness.doc: Metalness as grey; `metalness` then defaults to 1 and scales it.

emission.doc: Where and in what colour the surface glows (sRGB). Multiplied by `emission`, so set `emission` to white.

alpha.doc: Opacity as grey (white solid, black gone).

uvScale.doc: Repeats every map (and a procedural pattern) this many times across the uvs: [u, v].

uvOffset.doc: Shifts every map along the uvs: [0.5, 0] moves the picture half a tile toward −u.

uvRotation.doc: Turns every map on the uvs, degrees.

normalFlipY.doc: Flip the green channel of `maps.normal` (DirectX-style maps).

procedural.doc: A pattern baked into maps: wood, marble, tiles… See `procedural`.

screen.doc: Shows a video or a layer of the same project on the surface (a tablet, a TV, a billboard), over its UVs as a map: `url` or `layer`. It glows and lights the set in Final; the material's own fields still win.

url.doc: A video (MP4/MOV) or picture to show.

layer.doc: An item or channel id of this project: an HTML clip live from its page, a video in step with the timeline, an image.

shading.doc: `screen` glows; `lit` is the surface's colour under the set's light.

look.doc: A monitor: a glass coat with soft reflections over a near-black panel (Draft also gets a soft light from it).

roughness.doc: Roughness of the monitor's glass coat.

blackLevel.doc: How far the monitor's blacks are lifted.

light.doc: With look monitor: Draft's soft light from the screen (false leaves it out).

fit.doc: How the picture fits the surface.

offset.doc: A url video: seconds into it at the clip's start.

resolution.doc: An HTML page is laid out at this size, [w, h] px.

graph.doc: A texture graph: a smart material with wear and dirt. Give `preset` with its numbers beside it, or your own `nodes` and `out`; it is baked once into maps that Draft and Final both read. The graph checks its own presets, nodes and fields when the scene builds. See world3d.md, "Texture graphs".

preset.doc: A ready graph; its numbers go beside it in `graph` (each preset's numbers: world3d.md). Four are alive in time, the animated material pack: edgeGlow (light along the shape's edges), fractalNoise (3D noise that boils on the surface), motionBeam (a band of light travelling along the object), sweep (a band sweeping across it, as a glow or a sheen).

nodes.doc: Your own graph: `{ "op", "id", … }` nodes; a node's main input is the node before it unless given as "#id".

out.doc: What makes each map: base, roughness, metalness, height, emission, opacity ("#id", "#id.g", a number or a colour), heightScale, emissionStrength.

params.doc: Numbers your own nodes use as "$name".

keys.doc: Keys on the preset's numbers or your params, as an object's keys.

size.doc: The bake's width in texels. Left out, a per-object bake is sized for what the camera sees, a tiled one is 1024.

space.doc: "object": a bake per object, on an atlas of its own (wear and dirt make one anyway); "tiled": one bake over the uv, shared.

coord.doc: How the generators read the surface: the uv, the object from three sides, the world from three sides, or the atlas.

heightScale.doc: The relief in metres at height 1.

hold.doc: Seconds: a graph alive in time (edgeGlow, fractalNoise, motionBeam, sweep, or its nodes) stays at that moment, keys included, while the shot runs on.

reveal.doc: A surface that is there only between two frames, texel by texel (ink drawn on and wiped away). Written by a .blend import.

map.doc: The reveal map: each texel's rgb holds the two frames.

fps.doc: Frame rate the map counts in.

translucency.doc: Thin sheets that let light through to the other side: curtains, lampshades, paper, leaves. That share of the diffuse light passes, in `translucencyColor`. Make the sheet `doubleSided`.

translucencyColor.doc: Colour of the light that comes through a translucent sheet. Default: `base` with its map.

translucencyInner.doc: With `translucencyAttr`: the translucency where the group is 1 (the thick part); `translucency` is where it is 0.

translucencyAttr.doc: A vertex group (`group:thick`) that varies translucency across the mesh.

subsurface.doc: Light that goes into a body and comes out nearby: skin, wax, soap, marble, milk, jade (Blender's Subsurface Weight). Use a closed mesh. Wins over `translucency`.

subsurfaceRadius.doc: How far each of red, green and blue travels inside, before `subsurfaceScale`.

subsurfaceScale.doc: Metres that multiply `subsurfaceRadius`. Keep it small against the object (a few mm for a 10 cm thing).

iridescence.doc: A thin film on the surface: soap, oil, coated glass. Colours turn with the angle.

iridescenceIOR.doc: The film's own index: 1.33 soap water, 1.45 oil, 1.4 a lens coating.

iridescenceThickness.doc: Film thickness in nanometres (200 to 800 shows colours), or [min, max] for swirling bands.

iridescenceSeed.doc: Seed of the swirl of thicknesses when `iridescenceThickness` is a range.

metal.doc: A real metal: a name (gold, silver, copper, aluminium, chrome, iron, titanium) or { n: [r, g, b], k: [r, g, b] }. Sets metalness 1 and the colour, so leave `base` out.

metalN.doc: The conductor's n per channel (with `metalK`), instead of `metal`.

anisotropy.doc: Brushed metal: highlights stretch across the brush lines. 0.6 to 0.9 with roughness 0.15 to 0.3.

brush.doc: `linear` lines along `brushAxis`; `spun` circles around it (a watch dial).

brushAxis.doc: The brush direction (linear) or the axis of the circles (spun), in the object's own space.

roundEdges.doc: Metres: rounds sharp edges in the shading only, in Draft and Final (a thin highlight along each edge). 0.002 to 0.01 for 10 to 30 cm objects.

displacement.doc: Real relief: the mesh is subdivided and its surface moved along the normal by a height, (height - midlevel) × scale metres, as Blender's Displacement node (Displacement Only). The same moved mesh in Draft and Final, so the silhouette is the relief's too. The mesh needs uvs.

height.doc: The height: a picture's media URL (or `tex:<name>`), read raw (white 1, black 0) over the mesh's uv with the material's uvScale, uvOffset and uvRotation, as its maps are; or "pattern": the material's own `procedural` pattern's relief.

scale.doc: Metres the surface moves at height 1 (Blender's Scale).

midlevel.doc: The height that does not move the surface (Blender's Midlevel): 0.5 for a map whose grey is the surface; 0 pushes out only.

detail.doc: Metres: the longest edge the mesh is cut down to. Default: a 200th of the mesh's size. Smaller is finer relief and more triangles (each halving is 4 times as many).

maxTriangles.doc: The most triangles the displaced mesh may have; past it the detail stops short and `scene.warnings` says so. A scene's displaced meshes together stay under 1 600 000.

items.doc: A light in metres. `type` picks which other fields apply: sun (`dir`, `size`), area (`at`, `target`, `width`, `height`), spot (`at`, `target`, `angle`, `penumbra`, `radius`), point (`at`), and studio (a `preset` of several lights, sized to its `subject`). `at` and `target` may name an object to follow; `highlight` places a light by where its reflection must land. Any type links by tags: `lights`, `excludes`, `shadowFrom`, `shadowExcludes`.

id.doc: A name, unique among the lights. Keys and reports use it.

type.doc: The kind of light. `studio` is a preset of several lights (`preset`, `subject`).

color.doc: Light colour (sRGB), or a colour temperature as "3200K": a black body's colour at that many kelvin (1900K a candle, 2700K a warm bulb, 3200K tungsten, 5600K daylight, 6500K overcast sky), luminance 1 so `intensity` keeps meaning how bright.

intensity.doc: Strength. sun: irradiance like Blender's Sun Strength (3 is a bright day). area: radiance of the panel (the light leaving it straight out); a 0.5 m panel at about 1 m needs about 3 to 10. point and spot: candela-like, falling off with the square of the distance; 1 to 5 for a lamp about 0.5 m from what it lights. With `ies`: the intensity toward the profile's brightest direction. studio: scales all its parts (1 lights the subject as a studio would, whatever its size). Or give `power` or `lumens` instead.

kelvin.doc: Colour temperature in kelvin: the light's colour is a black body's at that temperature (times `color`, which stays white unless set). 1900 a candle, 2700 a warm bulb, 3200 tungsten, 4000 a cool white LED, 5600 daylight, 6500 overcast.

power.doc: Watts, as Blender counts them (its light's Power): point and spot give power / 4π per steradian, an area panel power / (π × its area). In place of `intensity` (which wins when both are given); a Blender light's Power carries over as it is. Not for a sun (its `intensity` is already W/m²). With `ies`: the profile's whole light.

lumens.doc: Luminous flux at 683 lumens per watt (Blender's): `power` = lumens / 683. A real bulb is dim at the default exposure (an 800 lm bulb is intensity 0.09): raise `exposure` as a camera would indoors, or use `intensity`. With `ies`: the profile's whole light.

castShadow.doc: false: this light casts no shadow (Draft and Final).

gobo.doc: Real geometry between the light and the set that casts a pattern of shadow (a window frame, blinds, leaves).

image.doc: A picture: dark parts block the light.

distance.doc: How far from the lit point toward the light the gobo stands, as a share of the way (spot/area) or of the shot's radius (sun).

rotation.doc: Turn about the light axis, degrees.

extent.doc: Width and height as a share of its distance from the light, instead of `scale`.

lights.doc: Light linking: this light lights only the objects with one of these `tags` (an object's parents' tags count). Left out: it lights every object. In Draft and Final alike; up to 15 lights in a scene may link.

excludes.doc: Light linking: this light never lights the objects with one of these `tags`: a key that must not spill on the backdrop, a rim kept off the table.

shadowFrom.doc: Shadow linking: only the objects with one of these `tags` throw this light's shadow; the rest let its light through. Left out: every object that casts shadows does.

shadowExcludes.doc: Shadow linking: the objects with one of these `tags` throw no shadow from this light (its light passes them), while still shadowing every other light and still lit by it.

group.doc: The light group for the light mix (`rig.look.lightMix`) and Final's light passes: lights of one group change together. Default: the light's own `id` (a studio preset's parts: the preset's id).

dir.doc: Points FROM the set TOWARD the sun (it need not be unit length). [0, 1, 0] is noon overhead; [0.4, 1, 0.3] a high sun front-right; y below 0 lights from underneath.

size.doc: Width of the sun in the sky, degrees: 0.5 the real sun (crisp shadows), 2 to 5 a hazy day.

highlight.doc: Put the light where its reflection lands on a chosen point of a glossy object, as the camera sees it: the renderer solves the mirror direction from the surface normal there (corrected for the surface's roughness) and places the light `distance` metres out, aimed at the point. It overrides `at` and `target` (a sun's `dir`), and is solved again when the object or the camera moves. Give `screen` or `point`.

object.doc: The object the highlight lands on.

screen.doc: Where in the picture: [u, v] from the top left, 0 to 1 (the camera's ray there must meet the object).

point.doc: Instead of `screen`: a point in the object's own space; the surface point the camera sees nearest it is used.

distance.doc: Metres from the point to the light. Default: the light's own `at` distance, else 2.5 times the object's size.

at.doc: Where the panel's centre is: [x, y, z] in metres; or "@id", the middle of that object's box; or { "object": id, "point": [x, y, z] }, a point in that object's own space. An object named here is followed as it moves (its keys, a sim's body): the light is placed again every frame.

point.doc: A point in the object's own space (its `at`, `rot` and `scale` apply). Left out: the middle of its box.

target.doc: The point the panel faces (it shines from `at` toward `target`, and only to that side): [x, y, z] in metres; or "@id", the middle of that object's box; or { "object": id, "point": [x, y, z] }, a point in that object's own space. An object named here is followed as it moves (its keys, a sim's body): the light is placed again every frame.

point.doc: A point in the object's own space (its `at`, `rot` and `scale` apply). Left out: the middle of its box.

highlight.doc: Put the light where its reflection lands on a chosen point of a glossy object, as the camera sees it: the renderer solves the mirror direction from the surface normal there (corrected for the surface's roughness) and places the light `distance` metres out, aimed at the point. It overrides `at` and `target` (a sun's `dir`), and is solved again when the object or the camera moves. Give `screen` or `point`.

object.doc: The object the highlight lands on.

screen.doc: Where in the picture: [u, v] from the top left, 0 to 1 (the camera's ray there must meet the object).

point.doc: Instead of `screen`: a point in the object's own space; the surface point the camera sees nearest it is used.

distance.doc: Metres from the point to the light. Default: the light's own `at` distance, else 2.5 times the object's size.

width.doc: Panel width, metres; it lies level (horizontal). The light is intensity × area, so halving it needs twice the intensity.

height.doc: Panel height, metres, along the panel's up.

circular.doc: A round panel (a disc `width` across) instead of a rectangle.

spread.doc: Degrees: narrows the cone the panel lights (a softbox with a grid). 180 is a bare panel. Keep the light on the subject by raising intensity by tan(h)/(tan(h)−h), h half the spread in radians.

texture.doc: What the light shines through or wears: `{ "image": url }` or `{ "pattern": "window" | "blinds" | "leaves" }`. A spot projects it; an area light wears it on its panel.

image.doc: A picture: its colours tint the light (a stained-glass window).

at.doc: Where the lamp is: [x, y, z] in metres; or "@id", the middle of that object's box; or { "object": id, "point": [x, y, z] }, a point in that object's own space. An object named here is followed as it moves (its keys, a sim's body): the light is placed again every frame.

point.doc: A point in the object's own space (its `at`, `rot` and `scale` apply). Left out: the middle of its box.

target.doc: What it points at: [x, y, z] in metres; or "@id", the middle of that object's box; or { "object": id, "point": [x, y, z] }, a point in that object's own space. An object named here is followed as it moves (its keys, a sim's body): the light is placed again every frame.

point.doc: A point in the object's own space (its `at`, `rot` and `scale` apply). Left out: the middle of its box.

highlight.doc: Put the light where its reflection lands on a chosen point of a glossy object, as the camera sees it: the renderer solves the mirror direction from the surface normal there (corrected for the surface's roughness) and places the light `distance` metres out, aimed at the point. It overrides `at` and `target` (a sun's `dir`), and is solved again when the object or the camera moves. Give `screen` or `point`.

object.doc: The object the highlight lands on.

screen.doc: Where in the picture: [u, v] from the top left, 0 to 1 (the camera's ray there must meet the object).

point.doc: Instead of `screen`: a point in the object's own space; the surface point the camera sees nearest it is used.

distance.doc: Metres from the point to the light. Default: the light's own `at` distance, else 2.5 times the object's size.

penumbra.doc: Soft edge of the cone, 0 hard to 1 soft.

radius.doc: Size of the bulb, metres: bigger is softer shadows.

ies.doc: An IES photometric profile (IESNA LM-63): how strongly the luminaire shines in each direction. The profile is the beam: a spot's `angle` and `penumbra` and a light's `radius` no longer apply. Its axis (0°, nadir) points at `target` (a point light: straight down without one). Brightness: `intensity` is the profile's brightest direction; `power` or `lumens` its whole light; none of them, a file's own candela (/ 683). In Draft and Final; its shadow is a point light's.

iesRotation.doc: Degrees: turns the IES profile around its axis. Aimed straight down, its C0 plane points along +z (toward a camera on +z) and C90 along -x, as in Blender; 90 turns C0 to -x.

target.doc: Only with `ies`: where the profile's axis points (its 0°). Left out: straight down. object.doc: The object the highlight lands on.

screen.doc: Where in the picture: [u, v] from the top left, 0 to 1 (the camera's ray there must meet the object).

point.doc: Instead of `screen`: a point in the object's own space; the surface point the camera sees nearest it is used.

distance.doc: Metres from the point to the light. Default: the light's own `at` distance, else 2.5 times the object's size.

radius.ignored: A point light has no size, in Draft or Final: its shadows stay hard whatever the radius. For a soft little lamp use a small `area` light with `circular: true` (or a `spot` with `radius`).

preset.doc: threePoint: key 45 degrees to one side and above, a big soft fill on the other side, a rim strip behind. topSoftbox: one big panel overhead and a low soft fill (food, cosmetics flat-lays, packshots on a table). rim: two strips behind, left and right, for an outline. bottleStrip: two tall narrow strips a little behind the subject's sides, the long clean highlight down each edge of glass, and a soft top for its shoulders. Each part is an `area` light `<id>.<part>` (key, fill, rim; top, fill; left, right; left, right, top).

subject.doc: The object the lights are sized to and aimed at (its box, children included). Left out: every object no wider than 2 m (floors and walls left out).

side.doc: Which side of the camera the key stands (threePoint), and the rest follow.

distance.doc: Scales how far the lights stand from the subject (1 is a studio's usual distance for its size).

lights.doc: The scene's lights, in metres (Rig lights are separate: `rig.lights`).

camera.doc: The scene's own camera (metres). With it the Camera layer has no say over the shot. Leave it out to film with the Camera layer.

at.doc: Where the camera stands.

target.doc: The point it looks at (the middle of the frame).

up.doc: Which way is up in the picture. Does not animate.

fov.doc: Vertical field of view, degrees: 20 to 30 a product shot, 40 to 50 a room. Taken on this frame, or on `frame` when the camera names one.

lens.doc: Focal length in mm on the `sensor` film (`sensorFit` says which side it spans); wins over `fov`. Keyable (a zoom).

sensor.doc: Film size in mm along the side `sensorFit` names (Blender's Sensor Width, or its Height for a VERTICAL fit). With `lens` it sets the view; with `fov` it sets the focal length, and so how much `fStop` blurs.

sensorFit.doc: Which side of the frame `sensor` spans, as Blender's Sensor Fit: "AUTO" the longer side, "HORIZONTAL" the width, "VERTICAL" the height. A portrait frame with "HORIZONTAL" (Blender's usual vertical film) has 36 mm across and 64 mm up at 9:16: its 85 mm lens blurs as Blender's does, where "AUTO" would read the same view as a 48 mm lens with about half the blur. Draft and Final.

frame.doc: The frame [width, height] in px that `fov` was taken on (a .blend import writes its render size). Rendered at another shape, the view is refitted as Blender frames it: the side `sensorFit` names keeps its view and the other follows the frame. Left out, `fov` is the vertical view of whatever frame renders.

fStop.doc: Depth of field (Final traces the thin lens; Draft blurs each pixel by the same lens's circle, up to a 12th of the frame's height): smaller is blurrier (1.4 very shallow, 8 deep). 0 or unset: everything sharp. The lens is `lens`, or the focal length giving `fov` on the `sensor` film (fov 28 at 16:9 on 36 mm across is about 41 mm), so the blur in pixels is a real camera's with that film, lens and f-number. On an orthographic camera (`projection: "ortho"`) the aperture is 1 / (2 fStop) metres in radius (Cycles' rule: f/10 is 5 cm) and a point blurs over aperture × |its distance / focus − 1| of the frame, the same at every place in it.

focus.doc: Focus distance in metres along the view; "@objectId" focuses on that object's own origin (its `at`, not the middle of its shape); { "object": id, "point": [x, y, z] } on a point in its own space. Default: the target.

bokehRotation.doc: Turn of the aperture shape, degrees.

anamorphic.doc: An anamorphic lens's oval bokeh: this many times taller than wide (1.33 to 2 as real anamorphic lenses; 1 round; below 1 wider than tall), its height the round bokeh's, as Cycles' aperture ratio. Final.

catEye.doc: Cat's-eye bokeh: toward the frame's edges the lens barrel cuts each out-of-focus highlight into a lemon shape pointing at the middle, as on a fast real lens wide open (0 off, 0.3 to 0.5 a vintage lens, 1 strong). Needs `fStop`; Final.

iso.doc: Physical exposure, with `shutter` and `fStop`: ISO 100, 1/50 s, f/4 is exposure 1, and each doubling of ISO or of the shutter time, or each stop wider aperture (`fStop` / 1.41), is one stop brighter. Only a camera that sets `iso` or `shutter` takes it: `fStop` alone stays depth of field. Multiplies the Rig's `exposure`; Draft and Final; keyable (an exposure ramp, an iris pull).

shutter.doc: Shutter time for the physical exposure: seconds (0.02) or "1/50". See `iso`. Exposure only (motion blur has its own settings). Keyable in seconds.

device.doc: A device preset: fills the camera's `autoExposure`, `noise` and `distortion` and the look's lens fields (`aberration`, `vignette`, `bloom`, `halation`, `localTone`) that the scene leaves out; every field the scene writes wins (0 included). "actionCam": an action camera taped to something moving (auto-exposure lagging 0.6 s, average metering, strong sensor noise, barrel distortion 0.2, chromatic aberration, vignette). "phone": a phone (fast centre-weighted auto-exposure, light noise, local tone mapping). "cinema": a cinema camera (no auto-exposure, a clean sensor, a little halation and vignette).

autoExposure.doc: Auto-exposure: the camera meters its own picture and opens up or stops down toward a mid grey, lagging behind as a real camera does (from sun into shade the picture stays dark for a moment, then opens up; out into the sun it blows out, then settles twice as fast). true takes the defaults (or the `device`'s). Draft and Final; the exposure at a frame depends only on the Scene's own clock, so a frame rendered alone is the frame inside a render. Scene camera only (a Camera layer filming the Scene has none). Its meter reads the Scene's set, model layers and the Rig's keyed lights as Draft lights them (not sims or 3D Text). The gain counts as ISO for `noise`.

lag.doc: Seconds the exposure takes to cover about two thirds of a change into the dark (into the bright it takes half that). 0.3 to 0.4 a phone, 0.5 to 0.8 an action camera, 1 to 2 a slow, dreamy adaptation.

strength.doc: How much of the way to mid grey it goes: 1 every view the same brightness, 0.8 to 0.9 as cameras do (dark places stay a little dark, bright ones a little bright).

min.doc: The most it stops down, in stops (a bright window, the sun in view).

max.doc: The most it opens up, in stops (a dark room, under a table).

metering.doc: What it exposes for: "center" weighs the middle of the frame most, "average" the whole frame alike, "spot" the middle tenth.

key.doc: The grey it exposes the metered average to (scene light after the exposure): lower is a darker camera.

exposureCompensation.doc: Exposure compensation in stops: with `autoExposure`, what it exposes for (+1 a stop brighter); without, the exposure itself. Keyable. Counts as gain for `noise`.

noise.doc: Sensor noise: grain in the light before the film curve that grows with the camera's gain (its `iso`, the compensation and the auto-exposure's gain) and toward the shadows, a fine luminance grain with coarser colour blotches, new on every frame. 0 off (the default), 0.3 a clean cinema sensor, 0.5 a phone, 1 an action camera. Unlike `look.grain` (film grain, even everywhere), it is nearly gone in sunlit parts and strong in the dark. Draft and Final.

distortion.doc: Lens distortion of the whole frame: above 0 barrel (a wide lens: straight lines bow outward, the middle magnified), below 0 pincushion (a long lens: lines bow inward); 0.05 to 0.15 reads as a real lens, 0.3 a fisheye-like look. The corners stay where they were, so nothing goes black. The picture, its depth and its masks bend together; Draft and Final.

projection.doc: A fisheye lens model: "stereographic" (an action camera's wide lens: lines bow, faces keep their shape; `fov` 72 is 116° across a 16:9 frame), "equidistant" (a classic fisheye, angles even across the frame), "equisolid" (a fisheye that squeezes the edges more). `fov` is its vertical view, or `lens` mm through the model. Final traces each pixel's ray through it (the middle keeps its full sharpness); Draft draws a straight lens that holds the corners (up to 80° off the axis) and bends it, softer in the middle the wider the lens. `distortion` adds its barrel on top. Not with `tilt`; no Draft lens blur (Final traces `fStop`). "ortho": an orthographic camera, for isometric product and architecture shots. Parallel rays: a thing is as big far as near, `orthoHeight` (metres) sets the frame instead of `fov`, and no depth of field unless `fStop` is set (then its aperture is 1 / (2 fStop) metres in radius, as Cycles' orthographic camera; Draft and Final). The camera still stands at `at` looking at `target`: nothing behind `at` is seen, so stand it back from the set. Draft and Final draw every edge on the same pixel. Not keyable.

orthoHeight.doc: The orthographic frame's height in metres (its width follows the video's aspect). Left out, the frame the perspective camera has at `target`. Keyable: a key on it zooms an orthographic shot.

shift.doc: Lens shift [x, y] in shares of the frame: the frame slides, the camera does not turn, so verticals stay vertical (a view camera's rise and fall). [0, 0.25] raises the frame by a quarter of its height to take in the top of a building from a level camera; x slides it right by shares of its width. Works with either projection; Draft and Final match. Keyable.

tilt.doc: Tilt-shift (Scheimpflug): the plane of sharp focus leans this many degrees off the film, hinged on the `focus` point (an object, the target, or the axis `focus` metres out). Positive leans its top away from the camera: 90 minus how steeply the camera looks down puts the whole ground in focus, near to far. Leaned far past that either way, only a thin band through the focus point is sharp and the blur grows steadily above and below it: the "miniature" look: about -85 to -88 for a tabletop a few metres off, -89 to -89.5 for a street seen from tens of metres (or the same positive), with `fStop` 1.4 to 2.8; the nearer to 90, the thinner the band, and it is thinnest with the focus point near the middle of the frame. Needs `fStop`. Final traces it; Draft blurs by the same lens. -89.5 to 89.5, keyable.

tiltRotation.doc: Turns the tilt's hinge about the view, degrees: 0 leans the plane top-to-bottom (a horizontal sharp band), 90 side to side (a vertical band). Not keyable.

of.doc: A field driven by a clock: { "clock": "move1", "map": [[u0, v0, ease], [u1, v1, ease], ...] } (or an expression of several: { "expr", "vars" }), or a list of such terms, which combine: `scale` multiplies them, every other field adds them (a logo that grows in on move1 and shrinks out on move2 is two terms). With keys on the same field the keys' value combines with them the same way.

clock.doc: The name of a clock in `scene.clocks`.

map.doc: The remap from the clock's value u to the field's value: [[u0, v0, ease], [u1, v1, ease], ...], u rising, v the field's shape (a number, or [x, y, z] for `at` and `rot`), ease the curve from that point to the next (any name or [x1, y1, x2, y2] a key's `ease` takes; `linear` for a part that should follow u exactly). Below the first u it holds v0, above the last the last v. Left out: the value is u itself.

expr.doc: Instead of `clock` and `map`: an expression of the Video Editor's ƒx language (the Custom ƒx's: + - * / ^, sin, cos, lerp, clamp, ...) over `vars` and `time` (seconds on the Scene's clock), as a Blender driver's scripted expression. A number, or [x, y, z] for `at` and `rot`: "[r * cos(a), 0.8 * r * sin(a), 0]", "(1.38 + 1.34 * z) * (1.015 - 0.003 * time)". One that does not parse or run is named in the render's warnings and leaves the field to its keys or its value.

of.doc: A number, or { clock, map }: that clock through its own remap.

clock.doc: The name of a clock in `scene.clocks`.

map.doc: The remap from the clock's value to the variable's: [[u0, v0, ease], ...], as a term's `map`. Left out: the clock's value itself.

vars.doc: The expression's variables by name: { "r": { "clock": "move1", "map": [[0.8, 0.06, "appleOut"], [0.97, 0]] }, "k": 2 }. A name the language already has (time, sin, PI, ...) is not a variable.

items.doc: One term: { clock, map }.

drive.doc: Fields driven by the scene's clocks: { "<field>": { "clock": "move1", "map": [[u0, v0, ease], ...] } } (or a list of terms), for the camera's keyable fields (a dolly out with the burst: `at`; a zoom: `fov`). See `scene.clocks`.

of.doc: One of the Video Editor's keyframe expressions (ƒx) on this field's keys, the very functions a layer's track runs: { "glide": "soft" }, { "spring": "snappy" }, { "wiggle": { "amp": 2, "freq": 1.5 } }, { "custom": "value + 0.02 * sin(time * 4)" }. One a field; a vector field takes it on each of its numbers.

elastic.doc: Elastic: reshapes each key's move into a springy one that overshoots and wobbles into place: { amp [100] %, freq [1.1] wobbles across the move, decay [5] }. true takes the defaults.

spring.doc: Spring: each key's move is a real spring in seconds: "snappy", "gentle" or { amp [100] %, freq [1.6] Hz, damping [0.55] }. true takes the defaults.

bounce.doc: Bounce: each key's move falls onto its value and rebounds in decaying hops: { amp [100] %, elasticity [45] %, bounces [5] }. true takes the defaults.

wiggle.doc: Wiggle: adds smooth noise around the keyed value: { amp (the field's own units; ten of its steps: 1 cm, 2 degrees, 0.02 of scale), freq [3] Hz }. true takes the defaults.

glide.doc: Glide: softens the keyed move (its eases included) through the editor's Glide: a fast response plus a slow tail, so it lands soft and keeps creeping on, never past the key and never back. A preset by name ("soft", "floaty", "trailing", "endless") or { fast [0.1] s, slow [0.6] s, weight [25] % of every move the tail carries, delay [0] s }. true takes the defaults.

weight.doc: Tail Share (%).

custom.doc: Custom: replaces the value with an expression of the editor's ƒx language (`value`, `time`, `frame`, `wiggle()`, `loopOut()`, `valueAtTime()`, `glide()`, ...): the text, or { code }. true takes the defaults.

fx.doc: The Video Editor's ƒx on a field's keys: { "<field>": { "glide": "soft" } }, for the camera's keyed fields.

env.doc: The scene's environment light and background. It merges over the Rig's own environment (`rig.env`).

hdri.doc: An .hdr panorama URL that lights everything. The Rig's presets live at /hdr/<preset>.hdr; without one the Rig's `env.preset` is used.

flat.doc: A plain environment of one linear colour [r, g, b] (no picture).

ambientTint.doc: Written by the editor from a Rig's Ambient and Hemisphere colours (at rest and keyed): linear [r, g, b] the environment is multiplied by, in place, or [sky r, g, b, ground r, g, b] for its upper and lower halves.

intensity.doc: Strength of the environment's light. 0.05 to 0.15 keeps a sun's shadows deep; 0.6 is a soft studio.

rotation.doc: Turns the panorama about Y, degrees.

keyDir.doc: Points FROM the set TOWARD where the panorama's key light comes from ([x, y, z], y up; need not be unit length): Draft's one directional shadow from the panorama falls from there instead of from the map's own brightest region. The footage call sets it from what the camera saw (a map made of a shot's frames, whose half-turn copy behind the camera would cancel the key's sideways part).

background.doc: What the scene shows where no object is: "env" the panorama, a colour ("#e9e4dc"), or "none". Unless `opaque` is true (or it is a colour), that part of the frame stays see-through and the layers below the Scene show there (the project background, black by default). Default: "env" when the Rig has no backdrop (cyclorama shape none), else "none".

opaque.doc: Fill the frame where no object is with the scene's own background (the panorama, or the `background` colour) instead of letting the layers below show: a sky through a window, a studio around a product. Glass in front of an empty background keeps its reflections only with it.

view.doc: The view out of the windows: a picture the eye sees where the sky shows (through an opening or a `pane`), at the picture's own resolution, in place of the lighting panorama there (a 1k panorama is blurred about 8 times through a window at 1080p). The room is lit by the environment as before: nothing that lights reads the view. Needs `background` "env". A plain photo of the street is a pinhole picture (`fov`, `dir`, `up`); a whole equirect panorama is `panorama: true`. Without a view the sky map shows, as before.

image.doc: The picture: any image the scene could use as a map (the media library's, an upload, a URL).

panorama.doc: true: the picture is a whole 2:1 equirect panorama, turned with the environment (`rotation`): the sky's sharper twin.

fov.doc: Degrees across the picture's width (a phone's main camera about 70, a wide lens 100).

dir.doc: Where the picture's middle looks, in the world: out of the window, e.g. [-1, 0.05, -0.4] for a window in a wall facing -x seen a little toward -z.

up.doc: The picture's up in the world.

intensity.doc: Brightness as a share of the sky it covers: 1 gives the picture the environment's mean brightness over the same directions, so it needs no exposure of its own.

haze.doc: 0 to 1: the picture's own mean laid over it, as dirty glass and the air across a street lay it: less contrast, the same brightness (0.15 to 0.3 for a view seen from inside).

distance.doc: Metres from the scene's origin out along `dir` to where the picture stands for an orthographic camera (`camera.projection: "ortho"`): its rays are parallel, so it sees the picture as a flat backdrop that far, as wide as `fov` makes it there; a window shows the part of it straight behind. A perspective camera sees the picture at infinity and ignores this. Nearer shows more of the picture through each window.

items.doc: A simulation: { "recipe": name, ...its params } or a whole sim/1 graph ({ "schema": "sim/1", ... }). Deep checks run when the scene builds; see sim.md.

sims.doc: Simulations: smoke, fire, cloth, liquids, particles.

items.doc: A flat picture or words standing in the world.

kind.doc: `image` with `src`, text, or `layer`: a layer of the editor's timeline drawn live on the card (the editor writes it for a layer standing in the world).

fontPx.doc: Text size it is drawn at, pixels.

weight.doc: Font weight.

height.doc: Height in metres (or of the frame with `screen`).

width.doc: Width in metres instead of height.

aspect.doc: A `layer` card's width over height, so it has its shape before the layer's first picture arrives.

at.doc: Position, metres.

With keys on the same field the keys' value combines with them the same way.

map.doc: The remap from the clock's value u to the field's value: [[u0, v0, ease], [u1, v1, ease], ...], u rising, v the field's shape (a number, or [x, y, z] for `at` and `rot`), ease the curve from that point to the next (any name or [x1, y1, x2, y2] a key's `ease` takes; `linear` for a part that should follow u exactly). Below the first u it holds v0, above the last the last v. Left out: the value is u itself.

expr.doc: Instead of `clock` and `map`: an expression of the Video Editor's ƒx language (the Custom ƒx's: + - * / ^, sin, cos, lerp, clamp, ...) over `vars` and `time` (seconds on the Scene's clock), as a Blender driver's scripted expression. A number, or [x, y, z] for `at` and `rot`: "[r * cos(a), 0.8 * r * sin(a), 0]", "(1.38 + 1.34 * z) * (1.015 - 0.003 * time)". One that does not parse or run is named in the render's warnings and leaves the field to its keys or its value.

of.doc: A number, or { clock, map }: that clock through its own remap.

clock.doc: The name of a clock in `scene.clocks`.

map.doc: The remap from the clock's value to the variable's: [[u0, v0, ease], ...], as a term's `map`. Left out: the clock's value itself.

vars.doc: The expression's variables by name: { "r": { "clock": "move1", "map": [[0.8, 0.06, "appleOut"], [0.97, 0]] }, "k": 2 }. A name the language already has (time, sin, PI, ...) is not a variable.

items.doc: One term: { clock, map }.

clock.doc: The name of a clock in `scene.clocks`.

map.doc: The remap from the clock's value u to the field's value: [[u0, v0, ease], [u1, v1, ease], ...], u rising, v the field's shape (a number, or [x, y, z] for `at` and `rot`), ease the curve from that point to the next (any name or [x1, y1, x2, y2] a key's `ease` takes; `linear` for a part that should follow u exactly). Below the first u it holds v0, above the last the last v. Left out: the value is u itself.

A number, or [x, y, z] for `at` and `rot`: "[r * cos(a), 0.8 * r * sin(a), 0]", "(1.38 + 1.34 * z) * (1.015 - 0.003 * time)".
