clock.doc: The name of a clock in `scene.clocks`.

map.doc: The remap from the clock's value to the variable's: [[u0, v0, ease], ...], as a term's `map`. Left out: the clock's value itself.

vars.doc: The expression's variables by name: { "r": { "clock": "move1", "map": [[0.8, 0.06, "appleOut"], [0.97, 0]] }, "k": 2 }. A name the language already has (time, sin, PI, ...) is not a variable.

drive.doc: Fields driven by the scene's clocks: { "<field>": { "clock": "move1", "map": [[u0, v0, ease], ...] } } (or a list of terms), for `at` and `rot`. See `scene.clocks`.

of.doc: One of the Video Editor's keyframe expressions (ƒx) on this field's keys, the very functions a layer's track runs: { "glide": "soft" }, { "spring": "snappy" }, { "wiggle": { "amp": 2, "freq": 1.5 } }, { "custom": "value + 0.02 * sin(time * 4)" }. One a field; a vector field takes it on each of its numbers.

elastic.doc: Elastic: reshapes each key's move into a springy one that overshoots and wobbles into place: { amp [100] %, freq [1.1] wobbles across the move, decay [5] }. true takes the defaults.

spring.doc: Spring: each key's move is a real spring in seconds: "snappy", "gentle" or { amp [100] %, freq [1.6] Hz, damping [0.55] }. true takes the defaults.

bounce.doc: Bounce: each key's move falls onto its value and rebounds in decaying hops: { amp [100] %, elasticity [45] %, bounces [5] }. true takes the defaults.

wiggle.doc: Wiggle: adds smooth noise around the keyed value: { amp (the field's own units; ten of its steps: 1 cm, 2 degrees, 0.02 of scale), freq [3] Hz }. true takes the defaults.

glide.doc: Glide: softens the keyed move (its eases included) through the editor's Glide: a fast response plus a slow tail, so it lands soft and keeps creeping on, never past the key and never back. A preset by name ("soft", "floaty", "trailing", "endless") or { fast [0.1] s, slow [0.6] s, weight [25] % of every move the tail carries, delay [0] s }. true takes the defaults.

weight.doc: Tail Share (%).

custom.doc: Custom: replaces the value with an expression of the editor's ƒx language (`value`, `time`, `frame`, `wiggle()`, `loopOut()`, `valueAtTime()`, `glide()`, ...): the text, or { code }. true takes the defaults.

fx.doc: The Video Editor's ƒx on a field's keys: { "<field>": { "glide": "soft" } }, for `at` and `rot`.

parent.doc: A scene object's id: the card rides it (its keys, drives and path), `at` and `rot` then an offset in its space, as a child object's are.

ignoreDepth.doc: Draw over everything instead of hiding behind objects.

receiveShadow.doc: A lit card that takes the set's shadows.

screen.doc: Pin to the frame instead: { x, y } in 0..1 from the top left.

layers2d.doc: Flat pictures and words in the world.

of.doc: One clock: a value (u, 0 to 1 by habit) keyed on the Scene's time, then run through `filter`. Every channel of one move reads the same clock through its own remap (`drive`), so they start, accelerate, glide and land together, each with its own ease.

items.doc: One key: `t` seconds on the scene's clock, `v` the value, `ease` the curve from this key to the next.

t.doc: Seconds from the Scene clip's start. A key before 0 starts a move already under way when the clip starts (an entry that is moving on its first frame).

v.doc: The value at `t`: a number or an [x, y, z] list, the same shape as the field it keys.

ease.doc: How the move from this key to the next eases. A name: the world's `linear`, `in`, `out`, `inOut`, `back`, `bounce` (cubic power curves), or any keyframe easing of the Video Editor, the very curve it plays, by id (`aeSmooth`, `aeIn`, `aeOut`, `natural`, `appleOut`, `smoothGlide`, `punch`, `power`, `expoOut`, `backOut`, `overshoot`, ...) or by the name its keys write (`AE Smooth`); `hold` stays on this key's value until the next key. Or your own curve, the editor's Custom: [x1, y1, x2, y2] as in CSS cubic-bezier(), x the share of the time between the keys (0 to 1), y the share of the move (-3 to 4: below 0 or above 1 overshoots).

keys.doc: The clock's keys: [{ t, v, ease }], v a number. Usually two: 0 at the move's start, 1 at its end, eased `smoothGlide` (fast out, a long glide, fast in).

filter.doc: An ƒx run on the keyed value, as on a key track: { "glide": "soft" } is the editor's Glide ƒx (Soft): the move lands softly and creeps on past its last key, never overshooting.

elastic.doc: Elastic: reshapes each key's move into a springy one that overshoots and wobbles into place: { amp [100] %, freq [1.1] wobbles across the move, decay [5] }. true takes the defaults.

spring.doc: Spring: each key's move is a real spring in seconds: "snappy", "gentle" or { amp [100] %, freq [1.6] Hz, damping [0.55] }. true takes the defaults.

bounce.doc: Bounce: each key's move falls onto its value and rebounds in decaying hops: { amp [100] %, elasticity [45] %, bounces [5] }. true takes the defaults.

wiggle.doc: Wiggle: adds smooth noise around the keyed value: { amp (the field's own units; ten of its steps: 1 cm, 2 degrees, 0.02 of scale), freq [3] Hz }. true takes the defaults.

glide.doc: Glide: softens the keyed move (its eases included) through the editor's Glide: a fast response plus a slow tail, so it lands soft and keeps creeping on, never past the key and never back. A preset by name ("soft", "floaty", "trailing", "endless") or { fast [0.1] s, slow [0.6] s, weight [25] % of every move the tail carries, delay [0] s }. true takes the defaults.

weight.doc: Tail Share (%).

custom.doc: Custom: replaces the value with an expression of the editor's ƒx language (`value`, `time`, `frame`, `wiggle()`, `loopOut()`, `valueAtTime()`, `glide()`, ...): the text, or { code }. true takes the defaults.

clocks.doc: Named clocks for motion design: { "move1": { "keys": [{ "t": 1.533, "v": 0, "ease": "smoothGlide" }, { "t": 3.4, "v": 1 }], "filter": { "glide": "soft" } } }. A field's `drive` reads one through its own remap, so every channel of a move rides one clock.

textureBudget.doc: Megabytes for all the scene's baked texture-graph maps: per-object bakes are sized down to fit it.

floor.doc: The ground's height, or null for none.

caustics.doc: Light focused through glass onto the set (Final). Unset: on by itself where it shows.

fog.doc: Fog, haze, dust or smoke evenly in the air of the set: a medium that scatters light, so beams show (a spot's cone, sun shafts through a window, a lamp's glow) and far things fade. Final traces it (the light it scatters, the shadows in the beams, the light it takes from what is behind it); Draft draws the same box through its lights. It fills a box (`min`, `max`), by default the one round everything in the scene: give a room's inside to keep it off the sky outside.

density.doc: How thick, per metre: a metre of fog takes 1 − e^(−density) of the light through it. 0.02 to 0.05 a faint haze, 0.08 to 0.15 a dusty room where a sun shaft reads, 0.3 and up a smoky club. 0 or unset: no fog.

color.doc: The share of the light it takes that it scatters back out, per channel (sRGB): white scatters all of it (bright fog), darker absorbs (smoke), a tint colours the beams.

anisotropy.doc: Which way it scatters: 0 evenly, 0.3 to 0.7 forward (dust, haze: a beam glows when you look along it toward the light, faint from the side), below 0 back toward the light.

bounces.doc: Final: how deep into a light path it still scatters. 1 lights it by the light that reaches it (shafts, cones, a lamp's glow); 2 to 4 adds its own light scattered again (thick fog softer and brighter). More costs time.

min.doc: One corner of its box, metres. Unset with `max`: the box round everything in the scene.

max.doc: The opposite corner of its box, metres.

volumes.doc: Baked smoke and fire from a .blend import. Live volumes are gone: use `sims`.

version.ignored: The Scene layer stores no version; nothing reads it here.

duration.ignored: The Scene clip's length on the timeline sets the duration.

fps.ignored: The project's frame rate is used.

look.ignored: The look lives on the Rig: `rig.look`.

exposure.ignored: Exposure lives on the Rig: `rig.exposure` (both modes) and `rig.render.exposure` (Final).

particles.removed: The old `particles` field is gone: use `sims`.

matter.removed: The old `matter` field is gone: use `sims` with an MPM recipe.

render.doc: How every render and still of the project films the Scene: `rig.render`.

mode.doc: draft: the fast raster look; final: path traced (seconds per frame).

spp.doc: Final: samples per pixel. 32 to 64 for a room with the radiance cache, 128 to 256 for glass close-ups.

diffuseBounces.doc: Final: how many times a path may bounce off a diffuse surface (matte paint, plaster, cloth), under `bounces`. 0 leaves diffuse surfaces their direct light only. Unset: only `bounces` limits it.

specularBounces.doc: Final: how many times a path may bounce off a mirror-like or glossy reflection (metal, a clear coat, the reflection off glass), under `bounces`. Unset: only `bounces` limits it.

transmissionBounces.doc: Final: how many times a path may pass through a surface (glass and liquid refraction, thin glass, translucent leaves and lampshades), under `bounces`. Different from `transparentBounces`, which counts cut-out alpha. Unset: only `bounces` limits it, and where see-through bodies nest or touch (a glass with its water and ice, a bottle and its liquid) a path's first 4 transmissions do not count against `bounces`.

volumeBounces.doc: Final: how many times a path may scatter in a medium (the scene's `fog`, a sim's smoke and fire), under `bounces`. 0 leaves fog and smoke their direct light only (single scattering: lit by every light, no light scattered on); 1 to 3 the soft glow of thick smoke and fog. Unset: only `bounces` (and the fog's own `bounces`, how deep into a path it still scatters) limits it.

transparentBounces.doc: Final: layers of glass a ray may pass through. Raise to 8 to 16 for nested glass and liquid.

glossy.doc: Final: blurs reflections of reflections so they do not sparkle.

clamp.doc: Final: caps one sample's brightness against fireflies; 0 is off. 10 to 50 helps speckles.

denoiseLook.doc: clean (the default) is the denoiser alone, smoothest; natural mixes a fifth of the traced picture back over the denoised one, so some grain and surface detail stay; raw shows the samples the denoiser read, without it, everything else of the trace unchanged (the denoiser still runs). For no denoiser at all use `denoise: false`, which also traces for none.

exposure.doc: Final only: scales the traced picture to match Draft or a Cycles frame.

draftShadows.doc: Shadows in the editor's Draft preview (renders always have them).

radianceCache.doc: Final: end paths in a cache of the room's light after the first bounce (faster rooms). false turns it off.

softReuse.doc: Final video: also carry the soft (matte) light of the frame before into each frame. Off by default: every video frame is steadied against the one before after the denoiser either way, and carrying the light makes each frame draw new samples, so the glossy and glowing parts boil. true for a shot whose light is nearly all matte (at least 9/10) and much of it lens-blurred, delivered at a high bitrate (ProRes): there it gives 7-19 % cleaner frames.

lightPasses.doc: Final keeps each light group's light apart (up to 6 groups, the environment and the glowing surfaces), so `look.lightMix` changes their strength and colour after the trace: a new mix is one denoise, not a trace. It turns the radiance cache and the video light reuse off for that render, and takes 16 bytes a pixel a group (33 MB a group at 1080p). Needs `denoise`.

passes.doc: Render passes: the Scene layer shows one of them instead of its picture, in the preview, stills and renders. Light passes (Final only; Draft shows the picture): "diffuse" (light off matte surfaces and the diffuse part of every material: direct and bounced), "specular" (reflections, refraction through glass, a clear coat, sheen), "emission" (what the camera sees straight: glowing surfaces, lights, the background); the three add up to the picture and are filmed with its curve and look. Data passes (Draft and Final, shown as they are, no curve or look): "albedo" (surface colour, unlit), "normal" (world-space normal as rgb = n × 0.5 + 0.5), "depth" (white near, black far, over `depthRange`; never blurred by depth of field), "objects" and "materials" (an ID colour each: the same name always the same colour), "mask" (white where `mask`'s objects or materials are, its edges their share of each pixel, as a cryptomatte: through depth of field and motion blur in Final). To use a mask on another layer without rendering it, give that layer a world matte instead (world3d.md, `trackMatte.objects`).

show.doc: Which pass the Scene layer shows.

depthRange.doc: For show "depth": [near, far] metres, white at near, black at far. Left out: from the nearest thing in view to 2.5 times the focus distance (the target).

objects.doc: Scene object ids; an object covers everything under it (its children).

items.doc: A Rig light (composition pixels, placed around the rig origin by azimuth, elevation and distance). See 3d.md. For lights in metres use `rig.scene.lights`.

lid.doc: Short id (letters, digits, - and _, up to 12). Keys use it: `sc:<lid>:<chan>`.

intensity.doc: What the subject receives, as a directional of this strength would give.

az.doc: Degrees around the vertical from +Z (the camera side) toward +X: 0 in front of the subject, 90 camera-right, 180 behind it.

dist.doc: Distance from the rig origin, composition pixels.

shadowSoftness.doc: Shadow softness (also the area panel's size multiplier).

texture.doc: A built-in `pattern` (window, blinds, leaves) or a picture `url`.

lights.doc: Rig lights. With `"renderer": "world"`, `[]` means none; left out, the default key, fill and rim (no shadows) light the scene.

cyclorama.doc: The Rig's backdrop (sizes in multiples of the composition height). `{ "shape": "none" }` for no backdrop.

mode.doc: solid colour, shadows only, or a picture.

light.doc: shadowCatcher: also takes the objects' light (their bounce and reflections) onto the footage's floor in Final, with `imageUrl` the floor's picture: 0 off.

env.doc: The Rig's environment (a preset HDRI by default). `scene.env` merges over it.

mode.doc: Shadow kind.

look.doc: The film look, applied after the render (never rebuilds the world). Unset fields: contrast 1.25, saturation 1.3, the rest 0.

grain.doc: Film grain: even over the whole picture, new on every frame. For grain that grows in the dark and with the camera's gain, the camera's `noise`.

whiteBalance.doc: The camera's white balance in kelvin: the colour of the light it takes for white. Unset (or 6500) changes nothing; 7000 to 8000 warms a room lit by an overcast sky (white walls with a faint warm cast, as interior photographers set it), 3200 to 4500 cools one lit by lamps.

localTone.doc: Local tone mapping, as an interior photographer's exposure blend: how much of the picture's large-scale brightness above `localToneKnee` stops over the scene's grey is taken out (0 off, the default), while its detail is kept: a window, its frame and the wall round it stop blowing out, the view outside reads. 0.7 to 0.9 for a room lit through its window; expose for the room.

localToneKnee.doc: Stops above the scene's grey that `localTone` leaves as they are: 2 keeps the room's own fall-off from its window and takes the window down; 1 flattens more.

localToneShadows.doc: How much `localTone` lifts the picture's large dark areas (more than the knee and a half below grey): 0 keeps a room's far corner as dark as it is. Default a third of `localTone`.

localToneDetail.doc: The detail kept over `localTone`'s base, scaled: above 1 a photographer's clarity (1.1 to 1.3), below 1 softer.

localToneContrast.doc: How much deeper `localTone` makes the picture's large-scale light under the knee: a room's fall-off from its window, its far corner darker, the detail kept (1 leaves it, the default; 1.2 to 1.4 for a window-lit room).

passMix.doc: Final: the light rebalanced by kind after the trace, as a compositor would from passes, without tracing again (a new mix is one denoise): each kind times its gain (0 takes it out, 1 leaves it). Draft is unchanged.

specular.doc: Times the reflections, the refraction and the coat.

emission.doc: Times what glows, the lights and the background the camera sees.

view.doc: The view transform, as Blender's: "agx" (the film curve, with `contrast` and `saturation`), "aces" (ACES 1.3's RRT and sRGB output: more contrast, highlights roll to white), "neutral" (Khronos PBR Neutral: colours exactly as authored up to near white, for product colours that must read true), "standard" (plain sRGB, clipping). `contrast` and `saturation` shape AgX only. Draft and Final.

lut.doc: A look-up table on the filmed picture: a .cube URL ("/media/…/look.cube", a 3D LUT from any grading tool), `{ "cube": "<the file's text>" }`, or a built-in grade: "tealOrange", "warmFade", "bleach", "cool", "mono", "identity". It takes the picture after the view transform (display sRGB) as grading tools expect. Draft and Final. A file that does not parse leaves the picture ungraded.

lutStrength.doc: How much of the LUT's grade (0 none, 1 all of it).

aberration.doc: Lateral chromatic aberration: red and blue fringes that grow toward the frame's corners, as from a real lens (0 off, 0.2 to 0.5 subtle, 1 about 0.8 % of the frame's half width at the corners).

tone.doc: `plate` films through sRGB alone instead of the film curve: for objects put into real footage (with contrast 1, saturation 1).

lightMix.doc: The light mix: each light group's strength and colour over what the scene's lights say, by group name (a light's `group`, or its `id`; a studio preset's id), plus "environment" and "emission" (the glowing surfaces; intensity only for those two). Draft takes it at once; Final with `render.lightPasses` mixes the finished trace again (one denoise); Final without traces again.

intensity.doc: Times the group's light: 0 off, 2 twice as bright.

color.doc: Tints the group's light (white leaves it).

exposure.doc: Exposure of the whole Scene (Draft and Final).

pose.doc: A model layer's pose (`model3dConfig.pose`): a character's clips, morphs, bones, constraints and layers, in one fixed order (`order`) that every render draws the same. With a pose, `model3dConfig.animation` only names the base clip when `clips` is empty.

order.doc: The pipeline's order, stored with the project: clips, morphs, bones, constraints, world. It is the only order there is; another is ignored with a warning.

items.doc: One of the file's animations, playing. The first clip is the base; each next one is laid over what is below by its weight (0..1): a crossfade is the next clip's `fadeIn` while the one before keeps playing. Before `start` and after `end` a clip lays nothing.

clip.doc: The animation's name in the file (the layer's pose report lists them). A name the file does not have is skipped with a warning, so a re-imported file keeps the pose.

end.doc: Layer seconds when it stops (null: never).

fadeIn.doc: Seconds it takes to rise to its weight after `start` (an S-curve, so the blend starts and ends gently).

fadeOut.doc: Seconds it takes to fall to 0 before `end`.

weight.doc: How much of it lies over what is below: 1 replaces, 0.5 is halfway.

time.doc: The clip's own time, set outright (key it to scrub the clip by hand); `speed` and `offset` then do nothing.

blend.doc: `add` lays the clip's change from the file's rest pose on top instead of replacing (a breathing clip over a walk).

clips.doc: The clips, the first one the base.

root.doc: Root motion: "normal" (the clip moves the character as it was made), "inPlace" (its travel along the ground taken out, up and down kept), "accumulate" (a looping clip carries on from where the last loop ended). Or { mode, bone } to name the root bone (left out: the top bone a clip moves).

mode.doc: The root motion.

bone.doc: The root bone.

of.doc: A morph target's weight, by name: a number, or { value, mode, weight, mesh, keys }.

value.doc: The weight it sets (0 none, 1 the whole target).

mode.doc: `replace` sets it over what the clips made; `add` adds to it.

weight.doc: How much of the control applies.

mesh.doc: Only on this mesh (by node name); left out: every mesh with a target of that name.

of.doc: A bone's (or any node's) local transform, by name, over what the clips and morphs made.

rot.doc: Rotation, degrees XYZ, in the bone's own frame (its local axes).

at.doc: Position in the bone's parent's units (`add`: an offset).

mode.doc: `add` turns, moves and scales on top of the animation; `replace` sets the local transform, blended by `weight`.

weight.doc: How much of it applies.

items.doc: A constraint, solved after the clips, morphs and bones, against the layer's world transform of this frame. `type` picks the fields: lookAt (aim a bone at a target), ik (two-bone IK: the bone's parent and grandparent bend so the bone reaches a target), parent (a bone held by a target), path (a bone moved along points), attach (a Scene object held by a bone).

bone.doc: The bone it acts on (attach: the bone that holds).

weight.doc: How much of it applies: key 0 → 1 to hand a bone from its animation to the constraint (space switching).

target.doc: What it looks at. "@id" (or "id") a Scene object, as it stands at the Scene's time; [x, y, z] a point in the Scene's metres (the editor's 3D space: one composition pixel is a millimetre); { "bone": "<name>" } one of this model's own bones.

bone.doc: A bone (or any node) of this model, by name.

chain.doc: How many bones share the turn, the bone and its parents (2: neck and head).

limit.doc: The most it turns from the animated pose, degrees.

axis.doc: The bone's front in its own frame. Left out: the model's front (+Z of the file, or `forward`) as the bone holds it at rest.

forward.doc: The model's front in the file's frame, for the default `axis`.

target.doc: What the bone reaches for (out of reach: the arm points at it, straight). "@id" (or "id") a Scene object, as it stands at the Scene's time; [x, y, z] a point in the Scene's metres (the editor's 3D space: one composition pixel is a millimetre); { "bone": "<name>" } one of this model's own bones.

bone.doc: A bone (or any node) of this model, by name.

pole.doc: Where the middle joint (elbow, knee) bends toward. Left out: the bend the pose already has. "@id" (or "id") a Scene object, as it stands at the Scene's time; [x, y, z] a point in the Scene's metres (the editor's 3D space: one composition pixel is a millimetre); { "bone": "<name>" } one of this model's own bones.

bone.doc: A bone (or any node) of this model, by name.

tip.doc: A bone under `bone` (a fingertip, a toe) that lands on the target instead of the end's own origin, so a hand touches what it reaches rather than going through it.

target.doc: What holds the bone. "@id" (or "id") a Scene object, as it stands at the Scene's time; [x, y, z] a point in the Scene's metres (the editor's 3D space: one composition pixel is a millimetre); { "bone": "<name>" } one of this model's own bones.

bone.doc: A bone (or any node) of this model, by name.

at.doc: Offset in the target's (or the bone's) frame, metres.

rot.doc: Turn in that frame, degrees XYZ.

items.doc: A point of the path. "@id" (or "id") a Scene object, as it stands at the Scene's time; [x, y, z] a point in the Scene's metres (the editor's 3D space: one composition pixel is a millimetre); { "bone": "<name>" } one of this model's own bones.

bone.doc: A bone (or any node) of this model, by name.

path.doc: At least two points (a smooth curve through them).

progress.doc: Where along the path, 0 its start to 1 its end (key it).

orient.doc: Turn the bone's front along the path.

axis.doc: The bone's front in its own frame, for `orient`.

forward.doc: The model's front, for the default axis.

object.doc: The Scene object (`rig.scene.objects[].id`, "@id" too) the bone holds. It is drawn there in Draft and Final; with `weight` below 1 it is part way between its own place and the hand.

at.doc: Offset in the target's (or the bone's) frame, metres.

rot.doc: Turn in that frame, degrees XYZ.

keep.doc: Hold the object where it was against the bone at the moment it is picked up (`grab`), instead of at `at`/`rot`: key `weight` 0 → 1 when the hand reaches it and it never jumps.

grab.doc: Layer seconds of the pick-up for `keep`. Left out: where `weight` starts to rise (the last 0 key before the first one above).

items.doc: An animation layer: its own clips, morphs, bones and constraints, each laid in its step over the pose below, by its weight, through its mask.

on.doc: false: the layer is left out (kept in the project).

weight.doc: How much of the layer lies over what is below.

mask.doc: Where a layer may write. Every list left out lets everything through. Bones and objects take their children too (`children: false` only the named ones).

bones.doc: Bones (and everything under them) the layer moves.

objects.doc: Nodes of the file by name (a mesh, a group), with what is under them.

exclude.doc: Bones or nodes (and their children) the layer never touches, inside the ones above.

Its own uvs are for patterns: a picture (`maps.base`) comes out upside down on its front and back and turned a quarter on the other four faces; for a picture use `decal`, `uvTriplanar`, or `uvPlanar` with the flips given there.

capsule.doc: `height` is the whole capsule, caps included.

lathe.doc: spins `[[radius, y], ...]` around Y. Either drawing direction works. A profile starting and ending at radius 0 is a closed solid; `closed` joins the last point to the first (a ring). `angle` is the sharp-corner limit: a bend sharper than it is a crease. `round` (metres) turns every corner of the profile into an arc, so a bottle whose shoulder is drawn as two straight runs shades as one smooth surface instead of a crease and a flat band: give bottles, jars and caps `round` 0.003 to 0.01 (for 10 to 30 cm), or draw the profile with enough points.

extrude.doc: pushes a 2D outline along Z. `depth` is the whole thickness, centred on z = 0. The bevel cuts into the outline, so the silhouette stays exact; keep it under half the thinnest stroke and under half the depth.

center.doc: With `svg`: centre the outline on the origin.

flipY.doc: With `svg`: flip y (svg y runs down).

holes.doc: With `polygon`: holes, each a list of [x, y].

size.doc: With `svg`: the longer side becomes this many metres.

tube.doc: Blender's curve with bevel depth. `path` is `[[x, y, z], ...]`, a spline through those points. `tension` 0 is the straight polyline.

ribbon.doc: a flat strip along a path. A source. Give its material `doubleSided: true`.

sdf.doc: solids that melt into each other like clay. A source. Each shape is `{ type, at, rot, ... }`, where `rot` is degrees, as on objects:

skin.doc: a body around a skeleton, Blender's Skin modifier. A source. `paths` is a list of branches, each `[[x, y, z, radius], ...]`; a branch that starts on another's point grows out of it. Or `points` with `edges: [[i, j], ...]` and `radius` as one number or one per point. Each bone tapers from one radius to the next and the joints melt together by `blend`. Ends are round. Use it for limbs, stems, cables with a bulge, creatures.

edges.doc: With `points`: bones as [[i, j], …] between points.

text.doc: Droid Sans Bold. `size` is about the capital height. Letters stand on y = 0 and run along +X. `align` is left, center or right.

inset.doc: a border `thickness` wide inside the picked region (each face its own with `individual`); `depth` moves the inside in (−) or out. `name` makes the inside a region (its own slot) for the next node; `sides` gives the border faces a slot.

along.doc: Read by the shared face-edit code; inset itself does not move along it (see extrudeFaces).

angle.doc: New faces shade smooth below this angle, degrees.

extrudeFaces.doc: moves the picked faces with walls joining them to where they were. `along`: `'region'` (the region's mean normal), `'normals'` (each point along its own, even thickness), or `[x, y, z]`. Negative pushes in: a recessed panel is `inset` with a `name`, then `extrudeFaces { region: name, distance: -0.003 }`.

angle.doc: New faces shade smooth below this angle, degrees.

loopCut.doc: rings of new edges where planes across `axis` cross the surface, `cuts` spread evenly or at the offsets in `at`. Nothing moves; it gives the next pick a line to stop at.

bridge.doc: joins two open loops with a band. With a pick, the picked faces go first and the holes they leave are joined (two facing panels make a tunnel); without, the mesh's own two open loops. Unequal loops zip with triangles.

angle.doc: New faces shade smooth below this angle, degrees.

weld.doc: merges points closer than that, drops collapsed and doubled triangles. Closes cracks between parts.

fillHoles.doc: caps open loops of up to `sides` edges (0 any), flat in their own plane.

angle.doc: New faces shade smooth below this angle, degrees.

name.doc: Makes the caps a named region for the next node.

recalcNormals.doc: turns every face the same way as its neighbours and every part outward. For imported or scripted meshes that shade black in patches.

setNormals.doc: hand-set normals on the picked faces (all if none): `smooth` (no hard edges), `flat`, `direction` (foliage cards facing up), `outward` from `center` (a soft bush), `cylinder` (away from the `axis` through `center`). Later ops keep them where the surface stays (moves, mirrors, booleans, unwraps, decals, edits elsewhere); ops that reshape it (`smooth`, `subdivide`, `bevel`, `remesh`) work them out again.

vertexGroup.doc: a named weight per point, 0 to 1, stored as `mesh['group:<name>']` (a Float32Array per vertex). `box`/`sphere` give 1 inside (`falloff: 'linear' | 'smooth'` fades a sphere to its edge), a `mask` its own value (`"P[1] * 2"`), the face picks keep their points. `mode`: set, replace, add, subtract, max, multiply. Ops that take a `group` read it; groups ride through every op, interpolated on new points.

seams.doc: marks where `unwrap` must cut: edges sharper than `angle`, edges with both points in a `box`/`sphere`/`mask` (draw a seam with a thin box), or the border of faces picked by `region`/`facing`/`group`. `mode: 'clear'` unmarks. Mark them right before the unwrap.

pins.doc: points `unwrap` must put at exact uvs (the mesh point nearest each `at`); a pick pins its points where their uvs are now. A piece with two or more pins is solved through them and not repacked. Four corners pinned to the picture's corners, with the picture's `aspect`, lay it exactly on a curved card.

clear.doc: Drop the pins set by earlier nodes first.

unwrap.doc: a conformal unwrap (least-squares conformal maps) with low stretch. It cuts at marked seams, edges sharper than `angle` and material borders, opens closed pieces and cone tips, splits any piece that would fold, overlap or stretch past `maxStretch`, gives every piece the same texel density and packs them into 0..1 with `margin` between (or across `tiles` UDIM tiles). Pictures read the right way round from outside (never mirrored); which way up a piece lies is the packer's choice, so pin it when that matters. `aspect` is the texture's width over its height: give it for a picture that is not square, or it lands squeezed. The result reports `mesh.uvStats`: `{ charts, l2, worst, angle, flipped, fill }`, where `l2` is texture stretch (1 is none; under 1.01 is invisible), `worst` the stretch 95 % of the area stays under, `flipped` folded triangles. Prefer it to `uvUnwrap`.

init.doc: How the solver starts: a projection or an unfolding.

iterations.doc: Solver iterations; the default grows with the mesh.

pins.doc: [{ "at": [x, y, z], "uv": [u, v] }]: points that must land at exact uvs (as the `pins` op).

rotate.doc: Let the packer turn pieces to fit.

udim.doc: uvs in UDIM tile 1001 + col + 10 · row become slot `material` + that offset, with uvs back in 0..1, so each tile is an ordinary material with its own maps, the same in Draft and Final: `"materials": ["tile1001", "tile1002"]`. Regions are named `udim1001`, `udim1002`, ….

uvTriplanar.doc: each face takes the picture from the side it faces most, in metres, all six sides the right way round (`uvBox` mirrors three). It switches sides at 45 degrees with no blend band; for one continuous map use `unwrap`.

decal.doc: - `box`: `at` is the label's middle on the surface, `normal` the way it faces; it reaches `depth` [half the smaller side] either side of `at`. For a box face or a flat panel.

shrinkwrap.doc: , `in: [what, onto]`: lays one mesh on another, each point to the nearest surface point taking its normal, or (`mode: 'project'`) along `direction` (`'normal'`: along each point's own normal). What finds nothing goes unless `keep`.

transform.doc: moves mesh, points and instances together. T * R * S, Euler XYZ like three.

weights.doc: A vertex group ("group:<name>") or a number that scales the op point by point: 0 stays put, 1 is the full op.

solidify.doc: adds thickness. -1 keeps the input as the outside and grows inward, 1 grows outward, 0 splits it. A sheet comes back a closed slab.

smooth.doc: recomputes normals, sharp above `angle`. This is Weighted Normal: big flat faces stay flat next to small bevels. `weight` is area-angle, area, angle or none. It changes shading only, never positions.

displace.doc: seeded 3D noise along the normals, up to `amount` either way. `scale` is noise frequency per metre. Subdivide first; it only moves the vertices that exist.

twist.doc: rotates slices around `axis`, -amount/2 at one end of the mesh to +amount/2 at the other.

weights.doc: A vertex group ("group:<name>") or a number that scales the op point by point: 0 stays put, 1 is the full op.

bend.doc: curls a mesh that runs along `axis` into an arc of `amount` degrees, keeping its length, turning towards `toward`. The middle stays put.

weights.doc: A vertex group ("group:<name>") or a number that scales the op point by point: 0 stays put, 1 is the full op.

taper.doc: scales across `axis`, unchanged at the low end and `1 + amount` at the high end. -1 is a point.

weights.doc: A vertex group ("group:<name>") or a number that scales the op point by point: 0 stays put, 1 is the full op.

wireframe.doc: every edge becomes a strut, with a ball on each joint. `thickness` is the strut's diameter. `quads` leaves out the diagonals of quads. The struts are separate closed shells that overlap, so `boolean` union them if a single skin matters.

array.doc: each copy is the last one moved by the same step, so offset + rotate makes a spiral. Real geometry: for thousands of copies use points and `copyToPoints`.

radialArray.doc: copies spun around `axis`, each first pushed out by `radius` (along x for the y axis).

mirror.doc: reflects across the plane through the origin and keeps both sides. `weld` (true or a distance) closes the seam and removes faces lying in the plane. Model the half with +x.

decimate.doc: fewer triangles. `ratio` is the fraction to keep; `error` caps surface movement as a fraction of the mesh's size. A closed solid stays closed, so a very low ratio stops above its target. Keeps uv seams.

uvBox.doc: per-face projection along the dominant axis. uv unit = 1/scale metres. The easy default for hard surfaces and patterns (wood, stone, fabric). Each face is projected as `uvPlanar` does along the axis it faces: top and bottom u = +x, v = +z; front and back u = +x, v = +y; sides u = +z, v = +y. So a picture comes out upside down on the front and back and mirrored on one side of each pair: for pictures use `decal`, or `uvPlanar` with the flips below.

uvPlanar.doc: flat projection. `fit` maps the bounds to 0..1, then `scale` (a number or `[u, v]`) and `offset` place that square. A picture's top row is at v = 0, and the axes run:

uvCylinder.doc: u wraps around `axis` `repeat` times, v is height * scale.

uvUnwrap.doc: a real atlas with no overlaps, uvs in 0..1, for baking. 65535 distinct points at most. `unwrap` (below) is usually better: seams, pins, less stretch, a stretch report.

subdivideLinear.doc: each triangle becomes four and the surface does not move. No smoothing: this is for `displace` to have vertices to push.

subdivide.doc: Blender's Subdivision Surface (Catmull-Clark). Triangulated quads are paired back first, so a box comes out round and even. `sharp` keeps edges sharper than that many degrees as hard creases (a box with `sharp: 30` keeps its outline and rounds nothing; use it with more `segments` for a soft box with crisp edges); picked points crease too. Each level is 4 times the triangles: stay at 2 or 3.

bevel.doc: Blender's Bevel with the Angle limit, on any edges sharper than `angle`, which is what makes a product catch light on its edges. `width` is how far it cuts into each face (the radius on a right angle). `segments: 1` is a chamfer; `profile` 0.5 is round, 0.25 a straight cut, towards 1 sharper, towards 0 a cove. A pick limits it to edges with both ends picked. Corners where three bevels meet are rounded properly. The mesh must be manifold where it bevels. Textured? `uvBox` after it.

inflate.doc: blows a closed mesh up like a pillow, a cloth with air in it settled to rest: puffy keys, throw pillows, balloon letters. `pressure` is the volume it ends at, as a multiple of the start; flat sides bulge and edges pinch. `shrink` (up to 0.3) shrinks the cloth before the air goes in, so it ends taut. Needs even triangles: a `box` with `segments` 16 or more, or `remesh` first.

damping.doc: How fast motion dies down while it settles.

deletePoints.doc: takes points away, and every triangle using one. `box` is `{ min, max }`, `sphere` is `[x, y, z, radius]`, and `mask` is an expression over `P`, `N`, `uv` and `noise` that is above 0.5 for the points to go.

wrangle.doc: runs on every point. `P`, `N` and `uv` are arrays to change in place, with `i`, `count` and `noise(x, y, z)` to hand: `"P[1] += noise(P[0] * 4, 0, P[2] * 4) * 0.1"`.

weights.doc: A vertex group ("group:<name>") or a number that scales the op point by point: 0 stays put, 1 is the full op.

assign.doc: gives picked triangles another material. Name them on the object: `"materials": ["paint", "chrome"]`, where the number is the place in that list. `name` makes the slot a named region that later nodes pick with `region` (a new name with no `material` takes the next free slot). Every op carries the slots on: ops that keep or split triangles exactly, and ops that build a new surface (`boolean`, `remesh`, `softUnion`, `decimate`, `wireframe`) by nearest surface. A slot past the object's `materials` list wears the object's own `material`.

remesh.doc: Blender's voxel remesh. The mesh comes back as an even skin of small triangles from the volume it encloses: overlapping parts become one body, long thin triangles become even ones, and sharp edges round off by about a cell. It needs a closed solid. Materials, region names and vertex groups come along; uvs only with `uv: true` (seams kept), else project again after it (`uvBox`). Do this before `inflate`, `displace` or anything that needs even triangles.

relax.doc: smooths the surface itself, Blender's Smooth modifier (`smooth` only changes shading). With `keepVolume` it softens without shrinking. Open edges stay put unless `boundary`.

weights.doc: A vertex group ("group:<name>") or a number that scales the op point by point: 0 stays put, 1 is the full op.

boolean.doc: , `in: ["#a", "#b", ...]`: union, subtract (the first minus all the others) or intersect. Every input must be a closed solid, so `solidify` a sheet first. Untouched surfaces keep their shading, uvs, materials and vertex groups; the cut is a hard edge and wears the cutter's material, or slot `cutMaterial`. Colours are dropped.

softUnion.doc: any closed meshes melted into one. About a second at 64.

drape.doc: the first input falls onto the rest and settles: a tablecloth, a throw over a chair, a sheet over a statue. The cloth needs vertices (`grid` with 48 to 96 segments). `floor` is a height it cannot pass. Inputs from `@object` arrive in that object's own space, so give the cloth the same placement or line them up with `transform`. The cloth does not collide with itself, and colliders thinner than two grid cells need a higher `resolution`.

damping.doc: How fast motion dies down while it settles.

project.doc: lays a mesh on another, like shrinkwrap. Each point drops to the first surface along `direction`, and points that miss go, unless `keep: true`. `offset` keeps it clear of the surface and `from` starts the ray further back.

keep.doc: Keep the points whose ray finds nothing.

merge.doc: , `in: [...]`: joins meshes, points and instances without cutting anything.

hair.doc: strands grown from the input mesh as real geometry, seen by raster and the tracer alike. `root` and `tip` colour each strand. `clumps` is how many guides they gather around, which is what makes hair read as hair. Stay under about 50,000 strands for a responsive Draft.

scatter.doc: random points on the input mesh, evenly by area, with N from the surface. Attributes: P N pscale orient Cd id, plus `uv`.

pointsGrid.doc: points on XZ with both edges included, x running first, row 0 at -Z. `count` is a number or `[x, z]`. `jitter` 1 moves a point up to half a cell.

pointsOnCurve.doc: even spacing along a spline. N and orient follow the tangent, so `align: "normal"` lines +Y up with the path.

attrib.doc: a wrangle, run once per point. In scope: `P N Cd orient` (arrays to write into), `pscale` (assign to it), `id i count`, `rand(n)` (0..1, per point; a different n is a different number), `noise(x, y, z)` (-1..1), and `attr` for custom attributes (`attr.kind = rand(1) < 0.5 ? 0 : 1`). Math works and is seeded. fetch, document, window, globalThis, process, Date and eval are undefined. Changing N re-aims orient unless the expression also sets orient.

copyToPoints.doc: instances of meshes on points, one instances entry per source. Input is the points, then the sources: `in: ["#pts", "#rock", "#tree"]`, or `in: "#pts", sources: ["#rock", "#tree"]`. `align` is normal (+Y along orient) or up (upright). `randomRotate: [x, y, z]` is degrees either way. `randomScale: [a, b]` multiplies pscale. `pick` is random or `attr:<name>` (a custom attribute, floored, modulo the sources). Cd becomes instance colour: linear RGB, multiplying the material's `base` (see `script` for converting a hex colour).

instanceRealize.doc: bakes instances into one real mesh, with colours in the optional `mesh.color` (3 per vertex). Use it before a modifier or boolean.

weightGradient.doc: 0 at `from`, 1 at `to` (default: the mesh's two ends on that axis). With `path`, the

mode.doc: How it combines with a group of that name already there.

ramp.doc: [[t, w], …] or evenly spaced [w0, w1, …]: remaps the weight.

weightProximity.doc: 1 within `inner` of a point or a path, 0 from

mode.doc: How it combines with a group of that name already there.

ramp.doc: [[t, w], …] or evenly spaced [w0, w1, …]: remaps the weight.

mode.doc: How it combines with a group of that name already there.

ramp.doc: [[t, w], …] or evenly spaced [w0, w1, …]: remaps the weight.

weightMask.doc: an expression over `P`, `N`, `uv`, `w` (the group so far) and `noise`, returning 0..1

mode.doc: How it combines with a group of that name already there.

ramp.doc: [[t, w], …] or evenly spaced [w0, w1, …]: remaps the weight.

weightSmooth.doc: blurs a group over the surface.

pad.doc: With no `box`: margin around the mesh, as a share of its size.

weights.doc: A vertex group ("group:<name>") or a number that scales the op point by point: 0 stays put, 1 is the full op.

sculpt.doc: holds the strokes as data. They stay editable, and they run again on whatever

spacing.doc: Dabs every this many radii, for strokes that set none.

weights.doc: A vertex group ("group:<name>") or a number that scales the op point by point: 0 stays put, 1 is the full op.

shapeKeys.doc: keeps the input as the basis and adds named poses

petal.doc: - It stands on its base at the origin and grows along +Y, its outer face toward +Z. u runs across (0 to 1) and v along (base to tip).

leaf.doc: the same op as `petal` with a leaf's defaults: a lance outline, a gentle arch back, a groove down the middle, a slight twist, and no tone (give `baseColor` and `tipColor` for one).

stem.doc: a closed tube that thins from `radius` to `taper` of it at the top (or follows `profile`, shares of `radius` base to top), then swells

drops.doc: water drops resting on the input surface (dew on a petal or a leaf, rain beading on a car, condensation on a bottle), as their own mesh in the input's space.

flowerHead.doc: - It is petals around +Y on the origin. `petals` is per layer, so the default is a tulip's six tepals in two whorls of three.

cup.doc: The petals' `cup`, written on the head (see petal).

curl.doc: The petals' `curl`, written on the head (see petal).

curlPower.doc: The petals' `curlPower`, written on the head (see petal).

flare.doc: The petals' `flare`, written on the head (see petal).

length.doc: The petals' `length`, written on the head (see petal).

midrib.doc: The petals' `midrib`, written on the head (see petal).

outline.doc: The petals' `outline`, written on the head (see petal).

ruffle.doc: The petals' `ruffle`, written on the head (see petal).

ruffleDepth.doc: The petals' `ruffleDepth`, written on the head (see petal).

ruffleFrequency.doc: The petals' `ruffleFrequency`, written on the head (see petal).

segments.doc: The petals' `segments`, written on the head (see petal).

thickness.doc: The petals' `thickness`, written on the head (see petal).

thicknessTip.doc: The petals' `thicknessTip`, written on the head (see petal).

tip.doc: The petals' `tip`, written on the head (see petal).

tipShape.doc: The petals' `tipShape`, written on the head (see petal).

twist.doc: The petals' `twist`, written on the head (see petal).

width.doc: The petals' `width`, written on the head (see petal).

room.doc: walls with thickness round `plan` (the inner corners `[[x, z], ...]`, either way round; wall `i` runs from corner `i` to `i + 1`), the floor and ceiling inside it, skirting along the walls (broken at doors), an optional cornice, and every opening's own parts. An opening is `{ wall, at, width, height, sill, kind }`: `at` is metres from the wall's first corner to the opening's middle, `sill` its bottom above the floor, `kind` `"window"` (defaults 1.2 x 1.4 at 0.9) or `"door"` (0.85 x 2.05 at 0). The wall is cut round it, so its reveals (the wall's thickness inside the opening) are real faces. `window` sets every window's `frame` [0.055], `depth` [0.07], `mullions` [[1, 1]] (panes across, up), `glass` [0.006], `sill` [0.025], `sillDepth` [0.18]; `door` sets `casing` [0.07], `leaf` [0.04] and `open` [0] (degrees). An opening's own `window` or `door` overrides them. Slots and `part`: `walls`, `floor`, `ceiling`, `skirting`, `cornice`, `frames` (window frames and door casings), `glass`, `sills`, `doors`, `portals`. Make one object per part you want (each its own material and its own texture bake); they all take the same plan.

window.doc: one alone, its bottom middle at the origin, the wall's inner face at z = 0 and the room toward -z. Window slots: `frames`, `glass`, `sills`, `portal`; door slots: `casing`, `leaf`.

door.doc: one alone, its bottom middle at the origin, the wall's inner face at z = 0 and the room toward -z. Window slots: `frames`, `glass`, `sills`, `portal`; door slots: `casing`, `leaf`.

curtain.doc: a curtain gathered into pleats on a rail at y = `height`, let fall and settled by the cloth solver with its top held (about half a second); `wind` blows it sideways (+x) while it settles; `steps: 0` hangs it unsettled, in even folds with a straight hem (a sheer cafe curtain on the lower panes). `natural` (0 to 1; 0.7 to 0.9 for a lived-in room) hangs it as cloth really hangs: the heading gathered into tight even pleats at the rail, the folds below of their own widths and depths, opening out and wandering toward a heavier turned-up hem, the leading edge swung back a little. Slots: `cloth`, `rail`. Give the cloth `doubleSided: true` (and a little `translucency` for linen against a window).

sofa.doc: (the same, 0.88 wide, one cushion): plinth, arms with a welt round their front panels, boxed seat cushions with a dent where people sit and stuffed back cushions leaning back (all piped), short legs. `lived` (0 to 1) is a sofa people sit on: softer seat cushions sagging deeper, each its own way, crowned and creased where people sit, piped, the back cushions slumped, and the arms' tops and fronts and the seats' front edges a shade lighter where they are rubbed (0.6 to 0.9 for a lived-in room). The rubbed parts are vertex colours, which show on an object whose upholstery is its only material: make the upholstery its own object (`part: "upholstery"`) and the legs another (`part: "legs"`). Slots: `upholstery`, `legs`.

armchair.doc: (the same, 0.88 wide, one cushion): plinth, arms with a welt round their front panels, boxed seat cushions with a dent where people sit and stuffed back cushions leaning back (all piped), short legs. `lived` (0 to 1) is a sofa people sit on: softer seat cushions sagging deeper, each its own way, crowned and creased where people sit, piped, the back cushions slumped, and the arms' tops and fronts and the seats' front edges a shade lighter where they are rubbed (0.6 to 0.9 for a lived-in room). The rubbed parts are vertex colours, which show on an object whose upholstery is its only material: make the upholstery its own object (`part: "upholstery"`) and the legs another (`part: "legs"`). Slots: `upholstery`, `legs`.

coffeeTable.doc: (1.8 x 0.9 x 0.75): a top on four tapered legs; `round: true` makes it a disc `width` across; `shelf` a lower shelf at that height. Slots: `top`, `legs`.

diningTable.doc: (1.8 x 0.9 x 0.75): a top on four tapered legs; `round: true` makes it a disc `width` across; `shelf` a lower shelf at that height. Slots: `top`, `legs`.

chair.doc: a wooden chair, its back at -z. Slots: `seat`, `frame`.

shelf.doc: an open bookcase; `books` (0 to 1) fills its shelves with books of their own size and colour (`palette: "muted"`: a real shelf's spines, mostly white, cream and black paperbacks and faded cloth, a few colours; `"library"`: a lived-in shelf's mix, a third white and cream paperbacks, the rest dark cloth and jackets (navy, black, oxblood, bottle green, slate) with a few ochres and greys; `"bold"` saturated cloth colours): two cover boards proud of a cream page block (seen from above), a spine with a title band or label on many, a few lying flat in stacks, one leaning on the end of a row. `spines: "real"` builds the books as a shelf holds them, for a room that has to pass as a photograph: real sizes (paperbacks, trade books, hardcovers and a few tall art books, runs of a series alike), spines toward the room a little in and out, a hardcover's rounded back with a coloured headband at head and tail and its boards proud of the pages, a paperback's flat back, the cloth worn lighter at the head, tail and hinges, and the lettering as type sets it: the title running down the spine in words of letters of their own widths, the author's name smaller below, a publisher's mark at the foot (a wide spine: the title across it), light on dark books, dark on light ones, gilt on some cloth; bigger books stacked flat at a row's end. The books carry vertex colours, which show on an object with one material: make the books their own object (`part: "books"`, a white `base` or a graph) and the boards another (`part: "boards"`). An object with `materials` wears no vertex colours, so its books would all be one colour. Slots: `boards`, `books`.

lamp.doc: a floor lamp, or `kind: "table"` (0.55 high, a turned base). The shade is an open, thin cone (top radius, bottom radius, height): give it `translucency` 0.5 to 0.8 and `doubleSided`, and put a `point` light at its middle (y = height - shade height / 2). Slots: `body`, `shade`, `bulb`.

rug.doc: a rug; `border` (metres) binds its edge with a band a little proud of the pile (slot `border`), `ripple` (metres, 0.003 to 0.008) lifts it in a few soft waves and `curl` (0.01 to 0.04) lifts its +x +z corner, as a rug that is walked on lies. `pile` (metres, 0.008 to 0.02 for a hand-knotted wool rug) stands a deep pile on it: its top lumpy where the tufts lean together, rolled down over a ragged edge that wanders a few millimetres. `fringe` (metres, 0.04 to 0.1) knots the warp's ends into tassels at its two short ends, lying on the floor each a little askew (slot `fringe`: give it a plain off-white wool, e.g. `fabric: { "weave": "knit", "threads": 900 }`). Slots: `rug` (the `woolRug` preset; `pattern: "lattice"` is the hand-knotted diamond lattice, and its `hand` (0 to 1, 0.6 to 0.8 for a real one) makes the lines wander further, swell, thin and fade here and there, and the ground drift in soft bands of dye, an abrash), `border`, `fringe`.

plant.doc: a pot with soil and a leafy plant: `stems` (about one per five leaves when left out) rise from the soil leaning out, with `leaves` on short stalks along their upper part, turning round each stem, larger and drooping more (`droop` 0 to 1) lower down, upright at the tip. `leaf` takes the `leaf` op's params (`outline: "oval"`, `ruffle`, `cup`...). The leaves carry colours (vertex colours): each leaf a shade of `leafColor` [[0.1, 0.22, 0.06], linear], young ones at the tips lighter, a paler midrib, a dry brown tip on `browning` [0.2] of the old ones. They show on an object of the leaves alone with a white material (`part: "leaves"`, `"base": "#ffffff"`, a green `translucencyColor`); the rest as a second object with `part: ["pot", "soil", "stems"]` (a list keeps those parts and their slots, so `materials` still lists all four). A floor plant is 30 to 50 leaves on 3 stems at 1.2 to 1.5 m; a sill plant 15 small ones on 5. `kind: "fig"` is a fiddle-leaf fig: leathery leaves wider toward their tip with a waist below, a sunken midrib and pale lateral veins (colours), a wavy edge, on stout petioles that arch up from the branch and bend down into the blade, and woody branches as thick as a thumb at the soil (give `stems` a bark brown); leave `leaf` out for its own leaves (what `leaf` sets wins; they are single sheets: a leaf with `thickness` takes a window's light through two faces and comes out much darker in Final). Use the same `kind` on both of the plant's objects. Slots: `pot`, `soil`, `leaves`, `stems`. Leaves want `translucency` 0.3 and `doubleSided`.

browning.doc: The share of the older leaves (0 to 1) that turn brown.

leafColor.doc: The leaves' colour, linear [r, g, b] 0 to 1; young leaves come a little lighter.

pictureFrame.doc: a frame with a mat and a picture, hanging from its back at z = 0 and facing +z. The picture's uv runs 0..1 across it (an image map, or a graph). For an image map give `upright: true`: the image then reads as drawn, seen from the front; without it the picture's v runs bottom to top and an image map shows upside down (the same as `uvScale [1, -1], uvOffset [0, 1]` on its material undoes). Slots: `frame`, `mat`, `picture`.

cushion.doc: a stuffed cushion: plump in the middle, thinning to a seam all round, its edges drawn in between pointed corners, faint creases from the corners, each `seed` a little uneven. `sag` (metres) presses a dent into its +z face where someone sat; `piping` (a radius, 0.003 to 0.006) runs a corded welt along the seam; `slump` (0 to 1) gives it weight, as a scatter cushion leaning on a sofa's back: its top flops forward with a soft crease across its front, its foot spreads and flattens (0.4 to 0.8 reads as a real cushion); `creases` (0 to 1) wrinkles its +z face where it was sat on: a few shallow valleys fanning round the dent and pulled toward its -y edge. It lies in x/y facing ±z, its middle at the origin: stand it on a sofa with the object's `at` and lean it back with `rot` [-15, 0, 0]; lay a seat cushion flat with `rot` [-90, 0, 0]. The sofa's own seat and back cushions are these (seats with a dent, all piped). Slot: `cushion`.

boxed.doc: 0 to 1: squares it toward a sofa's seat cushion: flatter faces, fuller edges.

throw.doc: a heavy throw (a wool blanket) dropped over a sofa's arm: across the arm's top (`over` wide, its top `height` above the floor), `inside` metres down the inner face toward the seat and the rest down the outer face, in soft heavy folds that grow from nothing where it rests on the arm to their full depth at the hem, the hem `drop` metres lower at one side than the other; every `seed` folds it its own way, with a real `thickness` all round. The arm runs along z (`width` no more than the arm is deep), its top's middle at x = 0, y = `height`, the seat toward -x: put the object's `at` at the arm's middle on the floor ([sofa x + width / 2 - arms / 2, 0, sofa z] for a sofa's right arm; `rot` [0, 180, 0] for the left one), `height` = the sofa's `height` × 0.78, `over` = its `arms`. Give it a knitted `fabric` and `doubleSided`. `fringe` (metres, 0.03 to 0.08) hangs tassels from both hems, each its own length and a little askew. Slot: `throw`.

script.doc: a JS function body that receives `(input, ops, ctx)` and returns a Geo or a MeshData (shapes below). `input` is the first input as a Geo. `ops` has every op above: `ops.box({ size: 1 })`, `ops.twist(geo, { amount: 30 })`, `ops.boolean(a, b, { mode: 'subtract' })`, `ops.merge([a, b])`; inputs first, params last, each returning a Geo. `ctx` has `inputs`, `params`, `seed`, `makeMesh({ position, index })`, `rand(i, stream)`, `noise(x, y, z)`. Same shadowed globals as `attrib`. Reach for it only when the ops above cannot say it.

procedural.doc: A pattern baked into tileable maps (colour, roughness, bump, and metal or glow where it has them) that Draft and Final both read. It follows the mesh's uvs; `uvScale` on the material repeats it.

scale.doc: Repeats per uv tile (whole numbers, so it tiles).

roughness.doc: A number or [min, max] across the pattern.

metalness.doc: A number, or [main, accent] for metal lines.

size.doc: Texture size in pixels (up to 2048 for close-ups).

emit.doc: The lines, grout or dots glow (0..1).

noise.doc: Fractal noise through the colour ramp: stone, plaster, sand, any soft mottling.
noise.unit: noise cells at the coarsest octave

contrast.doc: spreads the noise over more of the ramp

marble.doc: Polished marble: soft clouds, branching veins with a grey bleed, fine hairline veins.

veins.doc: main veins across a slab (whole number)

detail.doc: strength of the fine hairline veins

wood.doc: Wood: growth rings that close into cathedral arches, fine grain, open pores; optional boards.

rings.doc: growth rings across the tile (across one board when planks > 0)

figure.doc: how far the rings wander into arches

pores.doc: open pores in the earlywood (oak 1, maple 0)

planks.doc: boards across the tile, 0 for one continuous board

seam.doc: gap between boards, as a share of a board width

grid.doc: A cutting mat: major lines, fainter minor lines, slow mottling. Defaults match the Blender mat.

groove.doc: how far the lines are pressed in (0 = printed)

tiles.doc: Glazed square tiles: rounded edges, recessed rough grout, per-tile tone and tilt.

grout.doc: grout width, share of a tile

bevel.doc: edge rounding, share of a tile

wave.doc: unevenness of the glaze and of the tile planes

stagger.doc: offset every other row by half a tile

bricks.doc: Running-bond brick: chipped edges, kiln flashing, iron spots, recessed sandy mortar.

mortar.doc: mortar width, share of a course

checker.doc: Checkerboard with crisp anti-aliased edges, a slight per-square tone, optional grooves.

groove.doc: a pressed-in seam between squares (0 = printed)

dots.doc: Dots on a ground: raised glossy domes by default, holes with a negative relief, print at 0.

radius.doc: dot radius, share of the spacing

stagger.doc: offset every other row by half

brushed.doc: Brushed metal: streaks in colour, roughness and fine grooves along one direction.
brushed.colorRoles: ramp from dark streak to bright streak

direction.doc: the brushing runs along u or v

scratches.doc: Wear on a smooth surface: scratches mostly along one wiping direction, rough and slightly sunk.
scratches.unit: repeats (scratch density goes with its square)

length.doc: longest scratch, share of a repeat

cells.doc: Voronoi cells: cushioned stones or leather with grooved joints; negative relief gives hammered dents.

border.doc: joint width, share of a cell

relief.doc: cushion height; negative makes round hammered dents (use with border 0)

terrazzo.doc: Polished terrazzo: speckled binder packed with angular stone chips of several colours.
terrazzo.unit: repeats (chips shrink and multiply with it)

weave.doc: Woven fabric: round threads that arch over and dive under, twist, fibres, gaps. Plain, twill or basket.

gap.doc: space between threads, share of the pitch

veins.doc: Veins of a petal or a leaf over the sheet's own uv (the petal and leaf ops: u across, v base to tip; one uv tile is one sheet): a petal's fine veins fanning from its base and forking as it widens, or a leaf's midrib, side veins and the net between them. Veins darker and more saturated, their colour bleeding into the sheet beside them, a faint groove; a translucent petal shows them in the light through it.
veins.unit: sheets (1 for a petal or a leaf)
veins.colorRoles: sheet ramp from base to tip..., vein colour last

kind.doc: petal: veins from base to tip that fork; leaf: a midrib, side veins and a net

count.doc: petal: veins across the base; leaf: side veins on each side

fork.doc: petal: how often a vein forks as the sheet widens (0 never)

contrast.doc: how strongly a vein takes the vein colour

bleed.doc: the vein colour spreading into the sheet beside it

net.doc: the fine net of veinlets between the veins

along.doc: how much the sheet ramp follows the length (0: by soft blotches only)

blotch.doc: soft blotches of tone in the sheet

angle.doc: leaf: degrees between a side vein and the midrib

aspect.doc: leaf: its length over its width (sets the side veins' angle in uv)

vary.doc: petal: how unevenly the veins are spaced and how unlike in strength (0 even and alike, 1 a few strong among many faint)

wear.doc: a real sheet's wear: a ragged browned rim, soft water-soaked bruises and faint creases (0 none, 0.3 a fresh cut flower, 1 a tired one)

concrete.doc: Cast concrete: cloudy patches, sand, aggregate specks and air-void pinholes.
concrete.colorRoles: ramp from dark patch to light patch

curl_points.doc: Points in a box, carried by curl noise. The core demo: scrub it back and forth and the state hash repeats.

sparks_in_wind.doc: A fountain of hot sparks thrown up from a point, blown sideways by a gusting wind, bouncing on the ground and cooling as they die.

leaves_in_pulse_wind.doc: Leaves tumbling from above onto the ground, then swept up by pulses of wind: a radial burst from `pulseAt` at each pulse, gusts, and flutter.

pulse_explosion.doc: A fireball in pulses: each pulse throws fuel, heat and a burst of expansion from `at`; it burns, rolls up as a mushroom of smoke, and flings debris and sparks that the blast carries.

campfire.doc: A fire at `at` on the ground: flames licking up, a thin smoke above them, and embers lifted by the hot air.

smoke_column.doc: A column of smoke rising from `at`, curling as it climbs and leaning with the `wind`.

smoke_lines_grid.doc: A grid of thin lines (each a curve of many points) swirled by a hidden smoke flow: a vortex ring rising through it and side pulses, rolling the grid into dense, smoke-like strands.

streamers_in_explosion.doc: A pulse explosion that throws streamers: curves of many points shot out from the blast and carried by its flow, stretching and curling as the fireball rolls up.

cloth_drop_on_sphere.doc: A square of cloth dropped onto a ball: it falls, catches on the ball, slides and drapes into folds, its corners settling on the ground.

flag_in_explosion_wind.doc: A flag on a pole beside a pulse explosion: a breeze stirs it, then the blast's wind whips it out and it flaps hard, debris thrown by the blast punching it as they pass.

grains_on_cloth.doc: A sheet held at its four corners catches a block of sand dropped onto it: the sand splashes and heaps on the sheet, which dips and ripples under the impact. Sand and cloth push each other in one solve.

hair_in_wind.doc: Long strands growing from the top of a ball (a head): they fall over it, then gusts of wind and turbulence blow them out and back.

wall_shattered_by_pulse.doc: A wall standing beside a pulse explosion: the blast punches a hole in it and throws the pieces out (more, smaller ones where it hit), the smoke pours through and is pushed aside by them, and dust from their broken faces follows them down.

drop_and_shatter.doc: An object (a ball or a block) dropped onto the floor: it lands, cracks from where it hit, and breaks apart, the pieces skidding and tumbling, a puff of dust from their broken faces.

stack_topple.doc: A stack of crates (a pyramid, a wall of bricks or a tower) knocked over by a heavy ball thrown at it: they slide, tip and tumble down.

debris_swarm.doc: A blast throwing a swarm of small debris (GPU rigid particles: thousands of tumbling chunks) that rain down, bounce off a crate and the floor and each other, and settle flat.

pieces_through_curtain.doc: A block thrown through a hanging curtain: the cloth billows around it as it passes (rigid pieces push cloth), and it smashes against the wall behind, the pieces dropping back through the folds.

water_splash_with_debris.doc: A tank of water and crates dropped into it: they splash in, the light ones bob up and float, the heavy ones sink to the bottom. Water and crates push each other (the water pushes back on each crate with a force read back once a frame). Put a tank object (four walls, open top) at `at` with the inside `tank`.

water_pour.doc: Water poured from a spout into a glass (or, with glass: null, onto the floor): the stream falls, splashes at the bottom, and the glass fills. Put a glass object at `glass.at` (`radius` outside, `height`, a `wall` thick).

sand_pour_pile.doc: Sand poured from a nozzle onto the floor: it lands, spreads and builds a cone whose slope is its angle of repose (frictionAngle), sliding down its sides as it grows.

snowball_smash.doc: A snowball thrown at a wall: it flattens against it, cracks, and breaks into clumps that tumble to the floor (packed snow hardens; pulled apart, it breaks). Put a wall object at `wall.at` (`size`).

goo_drop.doc: A blob of goo dropped onto an object: it lands, spreads over it and sags, draping down its sides and stretching into slow drips (viscoplastic: it holds its shape under a little stress and flows under more). Put a sphere (or box) object at `object.at`.

big_explosion.doc: pulse_explosion grown: a bigger fireball in three pulses, in a box `scale` times the default's on every side (the same cell: res 384 is 96 at scale 1), so the cloud rolls up and climbs metres before it thins, and nothing is cut off by the box. The gas runs on sparse bricks: only cells with gas, heat or flow (and a brick round them) are held, in `memory` MB (the default explosion's dense box takes about 34; its textures 5.5 more, the bricks' atlas 7).

flood.doc: A wall of water let go at one end of a wide room: it slumps and runs across the floor, piles up against the scene objects in its way and flows round them (each one an object collider: its own triangles as a grid of distances), climbs the far wall and slops back. Over a million particles at the default res; the grid exists only where the water is (sparse bricks).

cloth_over_object.doc: A square of cloth dropped over a scene object of any shape: it catches on it and drapes into its hollows. The object collides through its own triangles (a grid of distances baked from them), so a ring, a chair or a statue holds the cloth by its real shape, not its hull; keyed, it moves the cloth. Name the object: `object: "<id>"`.

snow.doc: Snow falling through the set: soft flakes drifting down and swaying, melting as they reach the ground. Drawn as lit cards (the built-in snowflake texture): the scene's lights and shadows reach them and light comes through them from behind; `look: "sphere"` draws small lit balls instead.

dust_in_beam.doc: Dust in the air of a room, made visible by a beam of light (a sun through a window, a spot): fine motes drifting slowly in the air currents, catching the light where the beam crosses them and glowing when you look toward the light. Light the set with a beam and give the scene a `fog` for the air the beam itself shows in (world3d.md, Fog and haze: Draft and Final draw it through the lights and shadows). `haze` (0..1) adds a thin haze volume of the motes' own air instead (Final lights it by every light; Draft by the sun only, without the walls' shadows).

smoke.doc: Smoke rising from a point: puffs of smoke born at `at`, lifted and curled by the air, spreading and thinning as they climb, leaning with the wind. Drawn as a volume (the puffs splatted into a box of density each frame, which scatters and shades the light as a sim's gas does: lit by every light in Final, shadowing the set); `look: "card"` draws them as lit smoke-puff cards instead.

embers.doc: Embers lifted from a fire bed: glowing points thrown up from `at`, rising on the hot air, flickering on curls of it and cooling from yellow-white to a dim red as they die. They glow (bloom in the look makes them bloom) and in Final they are lights: the floor and walls round them take their light.

bokeh.doc: Bokeh: small glowing points (fairy lights, far city lights) hanging in the dark well behind the subject and drifting slightly. With the camera's `fStop` set and its `focus` on the subject, Final traces them into real out-of-focus discs (the lens's, not drawn circles; Draft stays sharp, as it does for every depth of field); in focus they are points of light. A long lens (a small `fov`) and a wide aperture make the discs big.

stars.doc: A starry sky: glowing points on a far dome round `at`, of many sizes, brightnesses and a few colours, still (keep `rig.look.bloom` low: stars are pinpoints). They are lights of their own (the sky stays dark), seen through windows and over a horizon; give the scene a dark `env`.

flock.doc: A flock of birds flying as one round a target (or along `path`): each keeps its distance, turns with its neighbours and holds to the flock (separation, alignment, cohesion through the neighbour grid), steers clear of the ground and of the scene objects named in `avoid`, banks into its turns and beats its wings; drawn as `look: "bird"` (a built-in bird with its own wingbeat), or your own model (`model`: a scene object's id; its GLB clip `clip` is the wingbeat). `land` brings a share of them down onto perches. Each bird is `size` m from wingtip to wingtip; a million of them is one bird and a million poses in Draft and Final.

program.doc: Your own simulation: points with your own attributes, born where your WGSL `init` puts them (or a scene object's own vertices, `on`), moved every substep by your WGSL `step` (neighbours in a radius, the scene objects' distance field, noise, keyed params), drawn as points, instances of a model, or the object's mesh moved by them. Fixed step, seed, checkpoints every second.

axis.doc: solid: the object axis the log runs along (auto: its longest side)

coord.doc: where the pattern is read: the uv (default), object space from three sides (no uv needed; object bakes only), the bake atlas, the coordinates of the node named in `at`, or world space from three sides (for what runs with the world's up: stains, drips; object bakes only)

figure.doc: how far the rings sweep into arches (flat-sawn cathedrals)

scale.doc: board widths per unit of the coordinate (leave 1 on boards; on an object, 1 / board width in metres)

seed.doc: another variant of the same pattern

solid.doc: per object: cut from a solid log by the object's own position, so end faces show rings and long faces the grain (no uv needed)
